  command whose root token never reaches a screen, the generate-root seed,
  the Coder automation's rotation credential, Portainer 2.45.2's
  self-created `local` environment. The Caddy token's client-IP filter now
  names both of the host's addresses, because the rebuilt host reaches the
  Cloudflare API over IPv6 and issuance failed until the `/128` was added;
  the token is rolled, not re-created, on a rebuild. Required inputs record
  a Cloudflare token naming rule (where it lives, what uses it, what it
  reaches) after the audit poller's token was revoked in place of the
  production-zone Caddy token on the cut-over evening; both corrected the
  same night, the poller reading again with 0 unexpected.
- **Lab DNS-01 by delegation into a dedicated lab zone (LAB-1, #948)**. Owner
  decision 2026-10-18: the lab zone is `hybridcloudinsights.com`, a domain the
  owner already held, connected to the same Cloudflare account that day
  (Free plan, nameservers moved at Hostinger, zone emptied). `infra-lab/dns.tf`
  adds `_acme-challenge.lab` and `_acme-challenge.coder.lab` as DNS-only CNAMEs
  to `_acme-challenge.lab.hybridcloudinsights.com` (variable
  `lab_acme_challenge_target`, output `lab_acme_delegations`, test asserts);
  `roles/caddy` gains `caddy_dns_challenge_override_domain`, rendered as the
  Caddyfile's `dns_challenge_override_domain`, because certmagic finds the
  zone for a challenge name by SOA walk and does not follow a CNAME. The
  runtime token is re-issued with DNS edit on the lab zone alone and rotated
  with `hcw-vault-set` + `bootstrap.sh`; the lab-host README has the token
  form, the forced-issuance proof (the stored certificate copied aside first,
  with the restore line) and the revocation of the production-zone token.
  Completed the same evening (21:04Z): the `hcw-lab` workspace applied the
  two CNAMEs once its VCS source was repointed to the moved repository (it
  had planned nothing since 2026-10-07), the token was rotated, a forced
  issuance obtained a new `*.lab.hybridcloudworks.com` certificate through
  the delegation, and the production-zone token was revoked; ADR 0032's
  LAB-1 interim is closed with the date. The Cloudflare DNS audit's
  `caddy-acme` allowlist entry is dated to match
  (`CADDY_PRODUCTION_ZONE_ACCESS_ENDED`, 2026-10-18T20:53Z, the minute the
  host switched tokens): a challenge TXT in the production zone from the
  lab host's address at or after that instant has no credential that could
  have made it and reads UNEXPECTED, with a regression test (CodeRabbit on
  #1280). Every other document that still said in the present tense that
  the token writes the production zone now says until when it did.
- **Cloudflare DNS audit: an apply that errored or was cancelled is still an
  apply (#948)**. The first live run of the apply-correlated `hcp-terraform`
  entry (2026-10-18 14:09Z) read 44 applies and still left four account-token
  edits UNEXPECTED — 2026-10-06 00:10Z and 2026-10-10 21:40Z, HCP Terraform
  runs whose apply stopped early after writing, which `filter[status]=applied`
  excluded. `fetchTerraformApplies` now reads every run, keeps each one whose
  apply began (`applying-at`) and closes its window at the first of
  `applied-at`, `errored-at`, `canceled-at` or `force-canceled-at` (the end
  of the read window for an apply still running); plan-only and discarded
  runs carry no `applying-at` and are skipped. The report names each apply's
  outcome.
- **Cloudflare DNS audit: the first live run's lessons (#948)**. The
  workflow's audit step caught the script's exit code on the command itself
  (the runner's `bash -e` ended the step before `$?` was read, so the first
  run failed instead of recording exit 2); a manual run can untick
  `open_issue` to report without escalating; and the report prints, for each
  UNEXPECTED change, the entry's shape (actor field names, request method,
  user agent; never values), because the first run showed the HCP Terraform
  token's edits arrive as `account/api_token` with no `token_name`. The
  allowlist is rebound to what the log carries: `hcp-terraform` is an
  account-owned token with the Cloudflare Terraform provider's user agent,
  not the lab host's address, **while an apply of `hcw/hcw-azure` was in
  progress** by HCP Terraform's own run record (read with the `TFC_TOKEN`
  secret; a user agent alone is a header anyone can send, as CodeRabbit
  noted); a new `terraform-owner-token` entry keeps
  the owner's own workstation `terraform` runs (the 2026-10-06 00:26Z
  edits) visible under their own name; `caddy-acme` is told by the lab
  host's address in the new `CLOUDFLARE_CADDY_HOST_IP` variable, the one
  address the token's client-IP filter allows, with the token name kept as
  a second key should the log ever carry it.
- **Cloudflare DNS audit: a daily poller of the account audit log stands in
  for the notification Cloudflare does not have (LAB-1 interim, #948)**.
  Owner decision 2026-10-18: Cloudflare has no notification type for
  audit-log or DNS-record events on any plan, so the interim for the Caddy
  token's DNS edit on the production zone is
  `.github/workflows/cloudflare-dns-audit.yml`. Daily at 05:50 UTC it runs
  `scripts/cloudflare-dns-audit.mjs`, which reads Audit Logs v2
  (`GET /accounts/{account_id}/logs/audit`, every page) from two hours
  before the previous successful scheduled run (at least 26 hours, at most
  14 days; manual runs do not move the resume point), so a failed run widens
  the next window rather than leaving a gap, keeps
  the create, update and delete events on DNS records in
  `hybridcloudworks.com`, and judges each against an allowlist carried at
  the top of the script with the reason for every entry: the
  `hcp-terraform-cloudflare-dns` token's edits, the Caddy token's `TXT`
  `_acme-challenge.*.lab` edits (an A record from it, or a challenge for a
  site name, is the finding), and the owner's own dashboard edits. An
  UNEXPECTED change opens `Cloudflare DNS audit: unexpected record change
  (<date>)`, labelled `Security` and `live-check`, or comments on the open
  one; a read that fails (no token, a non-200, a body that is not the
  `success: true` envelope, more than twenty pages) fails the run rather
  than passing quietly. Content-free: the token never leaves the
  environment, record contents are not read into the report, and e-mail
  addresses are masked. `scripts/cloudflare-dns-audit.test.mjs` covers each
  allowlist entry, the refusals, two-page reads, the non-200 and the empty
  window from hand-written fixtures in the documented shape. The runbook
  section is `docs/runbooks/edge-dns-verification.md`, "The daily DNS
  audit"; ADR 0032's LAB-1 bullet now names this as the interim. The owner
  steps are the `CLOUDFLARE_AUDIT_LOG_TOKEN` secret (*Account → Account
  Settings → Read*, the permission the endpoint accepts) and the
  `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` variable, with the two optional allowlist
  variables, in `docs/standards/required-inputs.md` §4.2 and §4.3.
- **CodeRabbit's approval is the required review (#972, option F)**. Owner
  decision 2026-10-18: `.coderabbit.yaml` turns on
  `reviews.request_changes_workflow`, so CodeRabbit requests changes while a
  finding is open and approves the head once every thread is resolved and
  its pre-merge checks pass, and sets `reviews.allow_author_approval: false`,
  so `@coderabbitai approve` from the author (sessions author as the owner's
  account) cannot stand in for it. The `Default` ruleset's `pull_request` rule
  takes `required_approving_review_count: 1` with `require_last_push_approval`
  by the owner's `PUT`; the rollback is the same `PUT` with the count at 0.
- **Lab host: a missing sshd drop-in keeps sshd on the loopback while the
  Arc agent is Disconnected (#1263 follow-up, CodeRabbit on #1263)**.
  - **The gap:** in its hold state, the Arc gate keeps sshd's bind as the
    drop-in has it. With no drop-in to read, it set
    `hardening_sshd_loopback_only` false, so sshd listened on every address
    while ufw's rule stayed held.
  - **The fix:** a missing drop-in now keeps the role's default, the
    loopback alone.
  - **Tests:** `tests/ufw-closed-ports.test.sh` covers the case, and stops on a drop-in it cannot read (55 checks).
- **Lab host: sshd's loopback bind follows the Arc gate, as port 22 does
  (#1257 follow-up, CodeRabbit on #1261)**. #1260 bound sshd to the loopback
  on every run. Opening 22 at ufw then no longer gave a path in, which broke
  two documented routes: a rebuilt host's onboarding over 22
  (`Register-LabArc.ps1`), and the Web Console reopen in "When Arc SSH is
  down".
  - **One decision:** the hardening role's new `tasks/arc_gate.yml` decides
    once, before `sshd.yml` and on every run whatever the tags, from the Arc
    agent. ufw's 22 rule and sshd's `ListenAddress` lines both follow it:
    closed and on the loopback while Arc SSH is ready, open and on every
    address while it is not, and left as they are while the agent reads
    Disconnected.
  - **The listener check:** `privilege_checks_public_tcp_ports` admits 22
    only on a run where sshd listens on every address.
  - **The arc role's guard:** it now also requires a live listener beyond
    the loopback before Arc SSH is turned off, and that listener must answer
    with an SSH banner.
  - **The `sshd -T` read-back:** while sshd should listen on every address,
    it requires an address beyond the loopback.
  - **Tests:** `ufw-closed-ports.test.sh` has 53 checks, with real listeners
    standing in for sshd and a bounded wait for each, and `sshd-apply.test.sh`
    has 24. The runbook's reopen now rebinds sshd too.
- **Lab host: turning Arc SSH off never leaves both SSH paths shut (#953
  follow-up, CodeRabbit on #1258)**. Port 22 has been closed at ufw while Arc
  SSH is ready since #1258. A run with `arc_incoming_ssh_enabled` false could
  close 22 in the hardening role, then clear the Arc agent's incoming ports
  later in the same run.
  - **Hardening:** `hardening_arc_ssh_wanted`, which follows that switch in
    `group_vars`, makes the gate open 22 in such a run.
  - **Arc role:** the new `tasks/ssh_off_guard.yml` refuses to turn Arc SSH
    off while ufw keeps 22 closed, as in a run narrowed to `--tags arc`. It
    reads ufw conservatively: an installed ufw must answer, any DENY or
    REJECT naming 22 refuses, and only a general allow from Anywhere counts.
  - **Tests:** `tests/ufw-closed-ports.test.sh` runs both halves against the
    real ufw (46 checks).

- **Lab host: sshd listens on the loopback only (defense in depth after #953 stage 3, #1257)**.
  - In `00-hcw-hardening.conf.j2`, added `ListenAddress 127.0.0.1` and `ListenAddress ::1` so sshd binds to the loopback alone.
  - On Ubuntu, `sshd-socket-generator` derives `ssh.socket`'s `ListenStream=` lines from these directives at `systemctl daemon-reload`; added `daemon_reload: true` to `Reload ssh` and added `Restart ssh.socket` handler.
  - Removed port 22 from `privilege_checks_public_tcp_ports` (`defaults: [80, 443]`), turning the loopback bind into a verified assertion in `tasks/listeners.yml`.
  - Added `listenaddress` checks in `tasks/sshd.yml` against `sshd -T`, updated `sshd-apply.test.sh` and `listeners.test.sh`, and updated documentation in `docs/runbooks/labs-host.md` and role READMEs.

- **Lab host: port 22 closed to the internet once Azure Arc SSH is ready
  (#953 stage 3, LAB-7)**. The hardening role's ufw tasks (now
  `tasks/ufw.yml`) delete the allow of each port in
  `hardening_ufw_closed_tcp_ports`, 22 on the lab host. A run then reads
  `ufw status` and fails if any ALLOW or LIMIT rule still names a closed
  port: alone or in a list, on any interface or address, or as Ubuntu's
  `OpenSSH` profile. `hardening_ssh_arc_gate` closes 22 only while the Arc
  agent is Connected with incoming connections on for port 22. While the
  agent is Disconnected (a drop, or a reset agent being onboarded again) it
  leaves 22 as it is. Otherwise, as on a rebuilt host that
  `Register-LabArc.ps1` onboards over 22, it keeps 22 open, and the run says
  which. `tests/ufw-closed-ports.test.sh` runs the tasks against the real ufw
  in a scratch network and mount namespace with a stub `azcmagent`, 36
  checks, in CI's `ansible-lint (lab-host)` job. `alert-lab-ssh-login` now pages any
  login that does not arrive through Arc (`lab_ssh_loopback_only` defaults
  to true). The query change is declared for the plan check, and Arc SSH's
  two applied creates are pruned from it. sshd still listens on every
  address behind ufw, so 22 stays in `privilege_checks_public_tcp_ports`
  until #1257 binds sshd to the loopback. The runbook adds "Closing port 22:
  the first run" and "When Arc SSH is down", the Web Console reopen.

- **Lab host: the play also fails if the host daemon publishes a port beyond
  the loopback (#958 follow-up)**. A socket read sees a published port only
  through Docker's userland proxy, a daemon setting. So
  `privilege_checks/tasks/listeners.yml` also reads the `nat` table's
  `DOCKER` chain, IPv4 and IPv6, and refuses any `DNAT` rule without a
  loopback destination. On 2026-10-17 the host's five rules were all
  `-d 127.0.0.1/32`. `tests/listeners.test.sh` now has 23 checks, and the check refuses a Docker firewall backend other than iptables, which its rule read does not cover.
- **Lab host: the play fails if anything listens beyond the loopback but sshd
  and Caddy (#958, LAB-12)**. The last check of every run
  (`roles/privilege_checks`, `tasks/listeners.yml`) reads every TCP and UDP
  listener with `ss`, the rootless sandbox's forwarded ports included.
  - **What fails:** anything not on `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1` or an IPv4-mapped
    loopback address, unless it is TCP on `privilege_checks_public_tcp_ports`
    (22, 80 and 443). The failure names each one.
  - **UDP and port 22:** no UDP port is public now that Caddy serves no
    HTTP/3, and port 22 leaves the list when it closes (#953, stage 3).
  - **The isolation chain:** the other half of LAB-12's acceptance is the
    host firewall's read-back (#1236), which fails the play when the live
    chains differ from the files.
  - **Tests:** `tests/listeners.test.sh` (15 checks, in the
    `ansible-lint (lab-host)` job). On the lab host's own `ss` output of
    2026-10-17 it refuses only Caddy's UDP 443, which the next bootstrap
    removes, and passes without it. The runbook gains "Listeners beyond the
    loopback".

- **Audit finding PLAT-8: Cosmos DB export immutability, dedicated state container, 90-day security log retention & PII data-plane auditing (#968)**.
  - Added time-based WORM immutability policy `azurerm_storage_container_immutability_policy.cosmos_export` in `infra/storage.tf` enforcing 35-day retention matching the `expire-cosmos-export` lifecycle policy so backup blobs cannot be deleted or overwritten by the application identity or non-admin roles. Parameterized locking via `var.cosmos_export_immutability_locked`.
  - Added dedicated mutable container `azurerm_storage_container.cosmos_export_state` (`cosmos-export-state`) for change-feed continuation tokens (`state/${container}.json`), preventing daily delta continuation token overwrites from failing against WORM container retention (`BlobImmutableDueToPolicy`). Updated `createExportBlobStore` in `functions/src/lib/backup/cosmos-export-edges.js` to route `state/` continuation blobs to `cosmos-export-state`.
  - Increased Log Analytics workspace retention from 30 days to 90 days via `var.logs_retention_in_days` (default 90) in `infra/main.tf` and `infra/variables.tf`, satisfying compliance retention requirements for diagnostics, security tables, syslog, and activity logs.
  - Enabled Cosmos DB `DataPlaneRequests` in `azurerm_monitor_diagnostic_setting.cosmos` in `infra/observability.tf`, with an ingestion-time table transformation (`azapi_update_resource.cosmos_data_plane_table`) filtering telemetry to personal data containers (`ambassador`), providing a compliant 90-day PII access audit trail without exhausting the workspace daily ingestion quota.
  - Documented quarterly out-of-subscription export strategy, immutability verification commands, and state container isolation in `docs/decisions/0028-cosmos-out-of-account-export.md` and `docs/runbooks/cosmos-restore.md`.
  - Added unit tests in `scripts/backup-immutability-retention.test.mjs`, `functions/src/lib/backup/cosmos-export-edges.test.js`, and updated `scripts/assert-expected-plan.mjs`.

- **Coder: one running workspace per learner, and cloud sign-ins kept in
  memory (#954, LAB-8)**. Owner decision 2026-10-16, in all three templates
  (`hcw-lab`, `amo-guided-lab`, `na-guided-lab`).
  - **Sign-ins in memory:** a 64 MiB tmpfs at `/tmp/cloud-creds` (0700,
    `noexec`, `nosuid`, `nodev`), with `AZURE_CONFIG_DIR`,
    `AWS_CONFIG_FILE`, `AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE` and `CLOUDSDK_CONFIG`
    pointing into it. A cloud sign-in never reaches the home volume, and
    ends when the workspace stops.
  - **One running workspace:** on a start build only, the template reads
    the owner's workspaces from Coder on the loopback with their session
    token (`hashicorp/http` 3.6.2, locked), failing closed unless Coder
    answers 200. A precondition refuses the start while another holds the
    limit: a start pending, starting, running or cancelling, or a failed
    stop. A failed start does not hold it.
  - **The launcher and the site:** a start refused for another lab names
    that lab, frames its Stop, and starts this one once the other stops. A
    `limited` state reads "Stop your other lab to continue", and the
    ten-minute cap does not run during that wait. The site's lab panel
    says one workspace runs at a time and a sign-in lasts until the
    workspace stops.
  - **Which builds it binds:** builds of a template version that carries
    it. Coder Community's dashboard Start rebuilds a workspace's own
    version, so the runbook has a one-time owner step after the first
    publish.
  - **Tests:** `template.test.mjs` (28) and `lab-host-launcher.test.mjs`,
    and the coder CI job now runs fmt, init and validate on every template.

- **Audit finding PLAT-6: Rebuild inventory outside Terraform, custom roles bootstrap, secret escrow & origin-secret rotation (#966)**.
  - Parameterized Azure custom role definitions: created `scripts/bootstrap-roles.ps1` and `scripts/bootstrap-roles.sh` allowing subscription ID injection (`-SubscriptionId`, `-ManagementSubscriptionId`) across all five custom roles (`keyvault-secret-writer`, `function-config-refresh`, `function-settings-reader`, `static-web-app-deployer`, `alert-rule-reader`), replacing hardcoded subscription GUIDs.
  - Added unit test assertion in `scripts/terraform-role-definitions.test.mjs` verifying that bootstrap scripts cover all registered custom role definitions.
  - Documented authoritative **Where to Re-obtain** paths in `docs/standards/required-inputs.md` §4.6 covering all 30 Key Vault secrets in `functions/src/lib/secret-catalog.js` (including portal URLs, CLI generation commands, Bitwarden item names, and auto-renewal tools). Updated §4.6b to document the five custom roles and bootstrap scripts.
  - Authored `docs/runbooks/origin-secret-rotation.md` detailing the 3-way lock between Key Vault `CF-ORIGIN-SECRET`, HCP Terraform `cloudflare_origin_secret`, and Cloudflare Transform Rule `x-hcw-origin-secret`, complete with zero-downtime execution order, verification curls, and rollback steps.
  - Authored `docs/runbooks/cold-rebuild.md` providing a single ordered, copy-pasteable disaster recovery guide from bare accounts to full production estate operation within the 8-hour RTO objective.
  - Updated `mkdocs.yml` navigation under `Runbooks:`.

- **Secrets: Google API keys and AWS price-list IAM access key auto-renewal (#1028)**.
  - Implemented automated Google Cloud API key renewal in `functions/src/lib/credentials/google-roll.js` via Google Cloud API Keys API v2 (`apikeys.googleapis.com`) with verify-before-delete semantics for `GEMINI-API-KEY`, `YOUTUBE-API-KEY`, and `GCP-BILLING-API-KEY`.
  - Implemented automated AWS IAM access key renewal in `functions/src/lib/credentials/aws-roll.js` using pure SigV4 signing (`node:crypto`) with verify-before-delete semantics for `AWS-ACCESS-KEY-ID` and `AWS-SECRET-ACCESS-KEY` scoped to `pricing:GetProducts`.
  - Enforced verify-before-delete: newly minted credentials are functionally probed against their respective cloud services (Gemini models list, YouTube videos list, GCP Billing services list, AWS Pricing GetProducts) AND committed to Azure Key Vault before old credentials are deleted. If a probe fails, the newly minted key is deleted and the existing key remains active and undisturbed.
  - Added CLI orchestrator `scripts/roll-cloud-credentials.mjs` supporting `--target <gemini|youtube|billing|google-all|aws|all>`, `--dry-run`, and `--check` modes with zero CLI argument secret leakage.
  - Updated `functions/src/lib/credentials/register.js` to set `renewal: 'automation'` with rotation commands for all five credentials.
  - Added 65 new unit tests across `google-roll.test.js`, `aws-roll.test.js`, `roll-cloud-credentials.test.mjs`, and `register.test.js`.

- **Coder: only the `lab-learners` team signs in, and no sign-in creates an
  account (#954, LAB-8)**. Owner decision 2026-10-16.
  - **The allowlist:** the `coder` role renders
    `CODER_OAUTH2_GITHUB_ALLOWED_TEAMS=HybridCloudWorks/lab-learners`, and
    `coder_oauth2_github_allow_signups` is `false`.
  - **The checks:** `tasks/signin_policy.yml` refuses an empty team list,
    or a team that is not `<organisation>/<team-slug>` in an allowed
    organisation spelled the same way, since Coder v2.38.0 checks a team
    only inside an organisation the learner already passed.
  - **Who is affected:** existing accounts, the owner's included, keep
    working, and the team is checked at each GitHub sign-in. A learner's
    first sign-in matches only an account the owner made with their
    primary verified GitHub email; the runbook's new "Coder sign-in:
    adding and removing a learner" has the lines, and a suspended learner's
    workspaces stop within a minute. Sign-ups off is the normal setting
    now, not a kill switch: `group_vars`, ADR 0032 and
    `docs/standards/required-inputs.md` say so.
  - **No account, no route:** sign-ups off does not cover a deployment's
    first account, which v2.38.0 lets through from GitHub or `/setup` and
    makes the Owner. Before Coder starts, the role counts the accounts in
    its database. With none, it takes Coder's Caddy route down and reloads
    Caddy then and there. Once Coder is up, a 404 from
    `/api/v2/users/first` fails the play. The runbook's "A Coder with no
    account yet" has the owner's measured recovery, and
    `scripts/lab-host-coder-first-user.test.mjs` holds it.
  - **Runbook token lines:** they strip the carriage return with
    `tr -d \\r`; one backslash had deleted every `r` from the token.
  - **Tests:** `roles/coder/tests/coder-signin.test.sh` (23 checks) in the
    `ansible-lint (lab-host)` job.

- **Secrets: Cloudflare API token auto-renewal via roll-token API (#1027)**.
  - Implemented automated Cloudflare API token renewal in `functions/src/lib/credentials/cloudflare-roll.js` and CLI orchestrator `scripts/roll-cloudflare-tokens.mjs`.
  - Supports all three estate targets: `tfc-azure-cloudflare-api-token` (`hcw-azure` HCP Terraform workspace), `tfc-lab-cloudflare-api-token` (`hcw-lab` HCP Terraform workspace), and `lab-caddy-cloudflare-api-token` (`vault_cloudflare_api_token` in lab host Ansible Vault).
  - Enforces verify-before-apply semantics: verifies the newly generated token secret against Cloudflare's `/user/tokens/verify` endpoint before committing to HCP Terraform or the lab host vault.
  - Updates HCP Terraform sensitive workspace variables via the JSON:API endpoint (`application/vnd.api+json`).
  - Updates the lab host Ansible Vault via `hcw-vault-set`, piping secrets strictly to standard input.
  - Updated `functions/src/lib/credentials/register.js` to set `renewal: 'automation'` for the three Cloudflare tokens.
  - Added 33 unit tests across `functions/src/lib/credentials/cloudflare-roll.test.js`, `functions/src/lib/credentials/register.test.js`, and `scripts/roll-cloudflare-tokens.test.mjs`.

- **Lab host: Azure Arc SSH as the owner's way in; port 22 stays open
  (#953, LAB-7 stage 2)**. Arc SSH carries the session through an Azure
  Relay connection the host's Arc agent dials out to, so sshd needs no
  inbound port. sshd still asks for the pinned key. Port 22 closes in a
  later change, once the owner has connected this way and through the
  Web Console.
  - **Azure:** `infra/lab-hybrid.tf` declares the Arc machine's default
    connectivity endpoint and its SSH service configuration, port 22 only
    (`Microsoft.HybridConnectivity` 2024-12-01). They are gated on the
    machine existing, grant no role, and are declared in the plan check.
  - **The host:** the `arc` role turns on the agent's incoming connections
    for port 22 alone. It fails closed unless the extension allowlist is
    still the Azure Monitor Agent alone, and the nightly drift check sees
    each setting. `arc_incoming_ssh_enabled: false` restores LAB-6's state.
  - **The desktop:** `Connect-Lab.ps1 -Arc` checks az, the ssh extension,
    the sign-in and the service configuration before writing anything.
    Its `ProxyCommand` helper gets fresh relay credentials on every
    connection, deletes them from disk before the connection starts, and
    passes them to the proxy in its environment alone. `HostKeyAlias`
    keeps the host key already accepted. Without `-Arc` the direct block
    returns.
  - **Docs:** ADR 0032's amendment of 2026-10-16, the runbook's "Connect
    through Azure Arc" and the architecture page.
  - **Tests:** `scripts/lab-host-arc-ssh.test.mjs` holds the port, names and
    api-version together across infra, the role and the script, and
    `Connect-Lab.Tests.ps1` runs the generated helper end to end against a
    stand-in az and proxy.
- **Lab host SSH: one user, one pinned key, public key only, behind a
  lockout guard (#953, LAB-7 stage 1)**. Port 22 stays open in this stage;
  Arc SSH and closing 22 follow.
  - **The key:** `group_vars` pins `hardening_admin_authorized_keys` to the
    owner's workstation key, and the `hardening` role writes `hcwadmin`'s
    `authorized_keys` from that list alone. Root's is emptied, and the
    copy-from-root fallback is gone.
  - **The guard:** before writing, the role stops on an empty list, an entry
    that is not one public key, or a list without the key of the most
    recent accepted login (read from 14 days of the journal).
  - **sshd:** a drop-in adds `AllowUsers hcwadmin`,
    `AuthenticationMethods publickey`, no agent, stream-local or tunnel
    forwarding (local TCP forwards stay), `LoginGraceTime 30`,
    `PerSourcePenaltyExemptList` for the loopback that Arc SSH will arrive
    from, and `LogLevel VERBOSE`. It is validated, read back with `sshd -T`
    and put back on failure. sshd is reloaded, never restarted.
  - **Order:** a pending-reload marker keeps root's keys until sshd has
    loaded the drop-in, even after an interrupted run.
  - **Connect-Lab.ps1:** stops writing root's `authorized_keys`, and
    prints the `group_vars` line that pins a key.
  - **Accepted risk:** passwordless sudo stays, with its compensating
    controls in the role README; hPanel's Web Console is the break-glass.
  - **Tests:** `admin-keys.test.sh` (33 checks) and `sshd-apply.test.sh`
    (21, as root) in the `ansible-lint (lab-host)` job, and
    `lab-host-ssh-hardening.test.mjs`. `lab-host-ssh-login-alert.test.mjs`
    now holds the pinned keys to the alert's fingerprints unconditionally.
- **Add-on images: SLSA build provenance attestation verification before pull (#1069, part 1)**.
  The `addons` Ansible role (`lab-host/ansible/roles/addons`) now verifies the
  SLSA build provenance attestation of each deployed add-on image against Sigstore's
  public transparency log and the expected GitHub Actions workflow identity
  (`attestation_identity_regexp`) using `cosign verify-attestation` before calling
  `docker_image_pull`. A missing attestation pattern, mismatched identity, or
  unreachable transparency log fails the run closed, preventing untrusted or
  unauthenticated images from being deployed. Sigstore `cosign` (v3.1.3) is pinned
  and SHA-256 verified in `bootstrap.sh` and `group_vars/all.yml` and tracked upstream
  via `scripts/lab-pins-upstream.mjs`.

### Fixed

- **AI Engine model refresh, routing display and cost reporting are corrected ([#1437](https://github.com/saulpatinojr/HCW-HybridCloudWorks/issues/1437)).** Provider lists refresh concurrently under one deadline per provider, incomplete pagination preserves the previous list, and routing reloads after catalogue changes. Planned tasks are distinguished from unavailable active tasks; unknown prices remain unknown, small costs remain visible, and Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS is the reviewed multi-speaker recommendation, with structured speaker annotations, verified promotional price expiry, and 25 output audio tokens per second; explicit saved selections remain intact. See [model review](docs/runbooks/ai-engine-model-review.md).
- **Ambassador links stay out of the public footer, and readiness respects qualification periods ([#1437](https://github.com/saulpatinojr/HCW-HybridCloudWorks/issues/1437)).** The hard-coded GitKraken Ambassador footer credit is removed. Application dates take precedence over recurring quarter/year windows in the dashboard and workspace; program details use the current upkeep period. Footer links wrap, program cards have more room, and ambassador dialogs and forms fit mobile screens.

- **A visitor lab session is saved as over only once Coder has confirmed the clean-up, and one Coder has not confirmed is kept and retried, not forgotten ([#1388](https://github.com/saulpatinojr/HCW-HybridCloudWorks/issues/1388)).** When a visitor pressed End session, or the sweep found a session past its hour, `functions/src/lib/labs/visitor-session.js` asked Coder to delete the workspace and the user, threw away whether Coder accepted, and saved the record as `ended` or `expired` anyway; nothing looked at it again, so a delete Coder refused was never retried. Coder deletes a workspace with a job that finishes later and refuses (HTTP 417) to delete a user who still has a workspace, so the user delete straight after an accepted workspace delete is refused for most sessions: a workspace that was never deleted keeps one of the host's 5 workspace slots, and the user stays behind. Found by two read-only reviews of the [#1383](https://github.com/saulpatinojr/HCW-HybridCloudWorks/issues/1383) fix, from the code and the Coder source and not run against a live Coder; the refusal of the user delete is not confirmed on the live host. Now a session is first claimed with a conditional write (`active` to `ending`, with a lease), so only one request calls Coder (two stops at the same moment make one set of Coder calls). It is saved as `ended` or `expired` only when both deletes are confirmed (accepted, or 404 or 410 because already gone). Otherwise it is kept as `cleanup_pending`, with which half is done (`workspaceGone`, `userGone`) so the workspace delete is not asked for twice, and tried again after 2, 4, 6 and 8 minutes by the sweep or by a later stop, then marked `cleanup_failed` after the fifth try, which nothing retries and which keeps its Coder ids for 7 days for a person to finish. A claim whose holder died is taken over by the sweep (or a later stop) after 5 minutes. The sweep (`reapExpiredVisitorSessions`) now also lists the waiting sessions, returns `{ reaped, finished, pending, failed }`, takes up at most 10 sessions a time, and runs from the status and start routes at most once a minute per worker. It runs only when someone visits (nothing else triggers it, and the status route answers before it sweeps while the switch is off), so a waiting record is kept for 7 days instead of the usual 2 hours; a timer that runs the sweep on its own needs the owner's decision and is in [#1403](https://github.com/saulpatinojr/HCW-HybridCloudWorks/issues/1403). A waiting session does not count as `active`, so the visitor is not shown it and may start another. A session is also no longer saved as over when the broker is not configured but the session has something in Coder to delete. A start that fails after Coder made the visitor's user (the workspace call timed out, which cancels only our wait while Coder can go on and make the workspace, or was refused) is now kept as a `cleanup_pending` note before the 502 is answered: the user's id and name and the workspace's name, no workspace id, no visitor hash (so no visitor can reach it), and a first try after 2 minutes. For a record with no workspace id the sweep looks the workspace up by owner and name (`GET /api/v2/users/{user}/workspace/{workspacename}`, [Coder's API reference](https://coder.com/docs/reference/api/workspaces), read 2026-10-26) and deletes it only when its name is the expected one and its owner is that user; one it does not find counts as gone for that try only, and the user delete, which Coder refuses while the user still has a workspace, is the confirmation. Every Coder call now has a timeout, 10 seconds for a delete and 30 for the calls that provision a session, so a hung Coder cannot hold a request open; ids are written into Coder's URL paths as one piece each. Logs say only what Coder answered for each half (for example `user HTTP 417`) and which try it was, never an id. Tests cover Coder refusing (500, 417, timeout, network failure), a later stop and the sweep each finishing it, 404 and 410 counting as done, the bound and the growing wait, the lease takeover, two stops and two sweeps at the same moment, a Coder that never answers, and the throttle; checked by ten changes to the code, the first of them putting the old behaviour back (each makes at least one test fail). `.azure/api-surface.json`, ADR 0032's amendment and `docs/runbooks/labs-host.md` (the statuses, a query for finding stuck sessions, numbered steps for finishing one by hand, rollback) describe it. Two independent reviews before the pull request found no wrong delete, no missed ownership check and no harmful second delete; what they found beyond this change (a delete build that fails after being accepted ends as `cleanup_failed`, a user create that got no answer leaves no note because its id is unknown, the 404 reading and the token fallback, and more) is in [#1403](https://github.com/saulpatinojr/HCW-HybridCloudWorks/issues/1403). Built on the [#1387](https://github.com/saulpatinojr/HCW-HybridCloudWorks/issues/1387) change. Not yet live: the owner deploys the functions. Keep `LABS_VISITOR_SESSIONS_ENABLED` off until then.
- **Visitor lab sessions now tell visitors apart: each visitor has their own daily limit and can read and end only their own session ([#1387](https://github.com/saulpatinojr/HCW-HybridCloudWorks/issues/1387)).** `functions/src/lib/labs/visitor-session.js` asked the client-identity helper for a `fromRequest` method that `createClientIdentity()` has never had (it has `anonymousKey(request)` and `trustedClientIp(request)`), so in production the lookup was skipped and every visitor was filed under the text `unidentified`. With `LABS_VISITOR_SESSIONS_ENABLED` on, that meant one shared daily limit of 2 for the whole site; `GET public/labs/visitor-session` answering any caller with the id and address of the live session (it has no Turnstile, origin or rate check); `DELETE ?sessionId=` then ending that session, and a new visitor being handed the first visitor's session; and Turnstile (Cloudflare's bot check) never being told the caller's address. Found by a read-only review of the [#1383](https://github.com/saulpatinojr/HCW-HybridCloudWorks/issues/1383) fix, from the code and not run against a live deployment; whether the setting is on in production was not checked. The three routes now read the caller the way `lib/labs/public-submit.js` does: `identity.anonymousKey(request).key` (a hash of the address Cloudflare reports) files the session and the daily limit, and `identity.trustedClientIp(request)` goes to Turnstile. A request that cannot be shown to have come through our Cloudflare (no origin secret), or that carries the secret but no usable client address (which the helper would otherwise hash into one shared bucket, the same fault under a new name), is answered `403 FORBIDDEN` before the store, Turnstile or Coder is used, and the log line says only that a request was refused. Only the helper's own refusal (its error now carries `code: 'ORIGIN_NOT_VERIFIED'`) is answered that way; any other error, such as a `TypeError` from a method the helper lacks, is thrown on and shows as a server error. The status route describes only the caller's own session. The stop route ends a session only for the caller it belongs to, and answers any other caller `404 Session not found`, the same words as for an id that never existed (or one that is already over), so holding an id is no longer enough. People behind one shared network address count as one visitor, as they do for every other anonymous limit here. A session already stored under `unidentified` can be neither read nor ended by anyone and is expired by the sweep when its hour is up. `createVisitorSessionHandlers` now refuses, when it is built, an identity without `anonymousKey` and `trustedClientIp` (`assertClientIdentity`, new in `lib/auth/client-identity.js`), where it used to carry on with no identity at all. **So the same mistake cannot come back unseen:** `functions/src/lib/auth/client-identity-calls.test.js` reads all of `functions/src` and fails any property read from an `identity` that the real helper does not have (the list of names is taken from the real object, not typed out), and any call of `anonymousKey`, `trustedClientIp`, `viaCloudflare` or `rateLimitKey` made with no request, naming the file and line; it also fails a test that writes its own `identity = { ... }` stand-in with a method the real helper lacks. The visitor tests, and the lab-start counter's tests in `visitor-session.counts.test.js` (which had copied the same stand-in), now build the real `createClientIdentity()` and send requests with the origin secret and an address, where they used to hand the code a stand-in that had the `fromRequest` method; new cases cover two callers (different keys, a daily limit each, Turnstile given each caller's address, neither able to read or end the other's session, nor to learn that a finished one existed), a request without the origin secret or without a client address, and a run of all three routes on an identity that throws on any property the real helper lacks, whatever the code calls it. Checked by putting the old lookup back (the identity guard and five visitor tests fail), taking the ownership check out of the stop route (four fail), letting an unverified request through as `unidentified` (four fail) and not giving Turnstile the address (one fails). `.azure/api-surface.json` and the visitor sessions section of `docs/runbooks/labs-host.md` describe the new answers. Not yet live: the owner deploys the functions. Keep `LABS_VISITOR_SESSIONS_ENABLED` off until this is deployed.
- **Ending a visitor lab session, and the sweep that expires old ones, now really save the session's record ([#1383](https://github.com/saulpatinojr/HCW-HybridCloudWorks/issues/1383)).** `functions/src/lib/labs/visitor-session.js` saved a changed session with `replaceDocIfMatch('lab_jobs', session.id, {...}, session._etag)`: an id, the document, then an ETag (the version stamp the database checks, so a write made from an out-of-date copy is refused). The real function in `cosmos-client.js` takes the whole document with its `_etag` inside it, then an options object, so both saves failed. The sweep (`reapExpiredVisitorSessions`) swallowed the error: an expired session stayed `active` and was never counted as reaped. The stop route (`DELETE public/labs/visitor-session`) deleted the Coder workspace and user first and then threw, so the visitor's "End session" ended in an error (the Functions host answers an uncaught error with HTTP 500) for a workspace that was already gone, and the record kept saying `active`, so the session still counted against the visitor limit (default 2) and starting again would hand back the dead workspace's address until the session's hour ran out. Not checked against a live deployment: this is from the code, the function's signature and tests that fail on the old calls. Both saves now go through one helper, `finishSession`, which calls `replaceDocIfMatch('lab_jobs', { ...record, status, endedAt }, { partitionKey })` and, when the save loses a race (a second stop, or the sweep, wrote first: a 412, or a 404 because the record aged out), reads the record again: already `ended` or `expired` means someone else finished it and the loser has nothing to do; still `active` means something else changed it and the save is tried again on the new version, up to three times, then the stop answers 409 and leaves the record `active`. A second stop of a session that is already over now answers `200 { ok: true, status: 'ended' }` without calling Coder again. The sweep now returns `{ reaped, failed }`; a save that fails for any reason other than a lost race, a record that keeps changing, a sweep that cannot list the expired sessions, and a Coder clean-up call Coder did not accept are each logged (by kind only: no session id, no error text, no Coder id) where the request has a log, which is the start route; the status route's background sweep still has none, because it runs after its answer is sent. Not changed here, and now visible: a session is saved as over even when Coder refused a clean-up call, and then it is not retried (before this fix the record stayed `active`, so later requests re-ran the deletes by accident); making the final status depend on a confirmed clean-up is [#1388](https://github.com/saulpatinojr/HCW-HybridCloudWorks/issues/1388). Also found by the review and filed separately, not fixed here: the code asks the client-identity helper for a `fromRequest` method that does not exist, so every visitor is treated as the same person ([#1387](https://github.com/saulpatinojr/HCW-HybridCloudWorks/issues/1387)); keep `LABS_VISITOR_SESSIONS_ENABLED` off until it is fixed. **So the same mistake cannot come back unseen:** `functions/src/lib/cosmos-call-shape.js` is the one definition of the shape `replaceDocIfMatch(containerName, document, options)` takes (a document object with a string `id` and the `_etag` it was read with; options only `{ partitionKey }`); the real `replaceDocIfMatch` calls it first and refuses any other shape with a `TypeError` that says what to pass and names no value, before the SDK is touched, and the shared test store `functions/test/memory-store.js` calls the same check, where it used to accept any argument order (the visitor tests' own store did, which is why they passed). I read the 37 calls elsewhere in `functions/src`; each passes a stored document (so one with its `_etag`) and `{ partitionKey }` or nothing, so none is affected. `functions/src/lib/replace-doc-if-match-calls.test.js` reads the source text and fails any `replaceDocIfMatch` call with more than three arguments, an id as its second argument or an ETag as its third, naming the file and line, so a call that no test reaches is still checked (it flags the two old calls, at lines 256 and 615 of the old file). The visitor tests now run on the shared store, with new cases for the save itself, the arguments the store receives, a second stop, the sweep winning or losing the race, a record that keeps changing, a record that aged out, two stops at the same moment, two sweeps at the same moment, and a store that cannot save. Checked by putting the old calls back (the visitor tests that save a session and the source-text test fail) and by taking the new check out of `replaceDocIfMatch` (the five tests that call it with a wrong shape fail). `.azure/api-surface.json` describes the stop route's answers. Not yet live: the owner deploys the functions.
- **Add-on follow-up to #1351: the status-route inventory names Cloud Crawler's
  setting, and the labs-host page stops saying the add-ons are not on the
  host**. CodeRabbit's two findings on #1351 were real and the PR merged before
  they were answered. `.azure/api-surface.json` now lists
  `ADDON_CLOUD_CRAWLER_URL` among the settings the status route reads and says
  it is not provisioned while the row is `coming`. In
  `docs/architecture/labs-host.md`, the Tool add-ons row says that "not yet on
  the host" was the state at the 2026-10-08 review and that all three add-ons
  answered on the live status route on 2026-10-24, and the Applied state row
  for ADR 0035 now records the merge dates (#1043 on 2026-10-09, #1089 on
  2026-10-12) instead of "not merged yet". **No host run date or commit is
  written**, because the repository does not hold them; the host's own record is
  still to be read (#1355). CodeRabbit's review of this pull request added two
  more corrections to the same page: a stale `[REVIEW REQUIRED]` marker on the
  ADR 0035 amendment is replaced by the owner's confirmation of 2026-10-10
  (#1044, ADR 0035 decision 8), and two statements that said more than the
  evidence are reworded: the status route showing an add-on answering is not the

- **Interviews: the header link moved to the Azure landing page, interview
  pages keep the Azure menu, and a route check that failed now passes
  (follow-up to #1337)**. CodeRabbit's two findings on #1337 were real, and
  a browser run found a third problem beside them. (1) The top menu is a
  fixed row of nine 100-pixel slots whose divider must sit in the same place on
  every provider; the tenth link #1337 added for Azure overflowed it at normal
  laptop widths and moved the divider. It was invisible on the live site
  because no interview exists yet, so it would have appeared the day the first
  one was added. The link is now an **Interviews** section on the Azure landing
  page (`/azure`), shown only once an interview exists, and the menu stays at
  nine links. (2) The header finds the provider from the URL alone, and
  `interviews` was not a known page type, so on `/azure/interviews` the Azure
  menu was replaced by the generic provider list. It is now a page type in
  `routeFactory.ts`, as `sandboxes` is for Docker, and the Azure menu stays on
  every interview page. (3) `npm run validate:routes` failed on two hard-coded
  `/azure/interviews/...` paths in a test; they now come from `interviewPath`.
  That validator is not run by CI, which is why nothing flagged it. Checked in a
  real browser at 1280 and 1100 pixels: nine links on every Azure page,
  interview pages included, the divider at the same position on all of them, no
  overflow, no errors.

- **The Linkie Hub follows Linkie's rename of profiles to pages**. An
  October 2026 notice from Linkie to API users says `GET /api/v1/profiles` is
  now `GET /api/v1/pages`, `/profiles/{id}/posts` is `/pages/{id}/posts`, the
  analytics parameter `link_in_bio_id` is `page_id`, and the key scopes
  `profiles:read` and `profiles:write` are `pages:read` and `pages:write`.
  Linkie's own API reference, read on 2026-10-23, shows the new endpoints, the
  `data.pages` list and the `page_id` parameter; the scope names come from the
  notice alone, because the reference does not list them. The hub's Links, Analytics and Settings
  tabs and the Connections test used the old names, and `linkieProxy`'s
  allow-list only let the old paths through, so they would have stopped
  working as soon as Linkie retired them. The allow-list, the frontend paths,
  the list reader (`data.pages`) and the analytics parameter now use the new
  names; the old paths are no longer allowed. The allow-list moved into
  `functions/src/lib/integrations/linkie-allowlist.js` so a frontend test can
  run every path the hub builds through the real matcher, and a rename that
  moves one side and not the other fails there (`ci.yml`'s frontend filter
  lists the two functions files that test reads, as the repository's CI-filter
  test requires). **The API key may need creating again**: a key that only has
  the old scopes answers 403 "Insufficient scope". Linkie's key form has three
  separate permissions, and the hub needs **Linkie pages** Read Only,
  **Automated posts** Read & Write and **Analytics** Read Only (a first draft
  of these docs asked for pages Read & Write alone, which would have passed the
  connection test and still refused posts and traffic; CodeRabbit caught it).
  `docs/standards/required-inputs.md` and the credential rotation schedule
  say how, with the exact Playground URL. Function names in the hub still say "profile"; a
  profile there is what Linkie now calls a page.

- **A healthy Functions deploy no longer goes red because the temporary
  firewall rule reached the origin one front end at a time**. The deploy opens
  an allow rule for the CI runner's address, and App Service applies it to its
  front ends gradually. The workflow waits for `/api/health` to answer, but a
  later request can still land on a front end without the rule and be refused
  with the platform's own 403 ("Ip Forbidden"). That happened on 2026-10-23
  (run 39997538990): health 200, the public content list 403, the detail read
  200, and the deploy failed after everything had been deployed and
  registered. `scripts/smoke-deployed.mjs` now sends every request through
  `originFetch`, which waits 5 seconds and tries again when, and only when, the
  answer is a 403 carrying the platform's `x-ms-forbidden-ip` header, for at
  most 90 seconds across the whole run. An app-level 403 (the admin guards,
  the CORS refusal) is never retried, because those checks expect it, and a
  firewall refusal can no longer make them pass for the wrong reason. A run
  that had to wait says so on one line. The script needs no redeploy to take
  effect: the workflow runs it from the repository.

- **The weekly bump no longer lets kubectl run ahead of the Kubernetes
  schemas kubeconform checks against (#1323)**. The lab image pins kubectl
  (`KUBECTL_VERSION`) and a copy of the Kubernetes JSON schemas
  (`KUBERNETES_JSON_SCHEMA_*`) that are meant to sit on the same Kubernetes
  line, but the weekly bump only ever edited kubectl, so the first new line
  would have left kubeconform validating against the old API with a green
  build. The schema pins are a commit and a tree hash that no publisher
  serves a checksum for, so a bot cannot move them with kubectl. The bump now
  takes kubectl's patch releases from the pinned line's own pointer
  (`stable-1.37.txt`) and, when `stable.txt` names a newer line, adds a
  "Kubernetes release line" note to the weekly issue instead of moving
  kubectl: the line is moved by hand, kubectl and the schemas in one pull
  request. A test fails when `KUBERNETES_JSON_SCHEMA_DIR` and
  `KUBECTL_VERSION` are on different lines, so a hand bump that moves one
  fails in CI. Patch releases stay green because the check is on the line, not
  the patch number. Six new cases in `lab-pin-bumps.test.mjs`; breaking the
  planner or the pins five ways turned them red.
- **A Docker upgrade no longer leaves Portainer's `local` environment down
  until someone restarts the container (#1328)**. Portainer holds the Docker
  socket as a bind-mounted file, so when Docker restarts (any docker-ce
  upgrade does) a Portainer that was already running keeps the old, deleted
  socket: it still answers, but it can no longer see this host's Docker. The
  2026-10-21 bootstrap (Docker 29.9.1 to 29.9.2, #1324) left it so, the
  15-minute check failed three times in a row and raised the lab alert, and
  `sudo docker restart portainer` was the cure. The agent's socket proxy had
  the same fault in #1135. The `portainer` role now installs the `labs_agent`
  role's `hcw-docker-proxy-stale` helper (the same file, to the same path, so
  there is one copy to keep right) and asks it whether Portainer started
  before the daemon's current start. If it did, the container task restarts
  it onto the new socket and the run says so; if it did not, nothing is
  restarted. The weekly run proposes Docker upgrades, so without this it
  would have come back each time. `portainer-stale-socket.test.sh` holds the
  wiring (the restart tied to the answer and not to every run, asked before
  the container task, skipped in check mode, one helper file for both roles)
  and runs the helper against stand-ins for `systemctl` and `docker` with this
  role's own container name; putting each of eight breaks back in turn turned
  it red. CI runs it in the `ansible-lint (lab-host)` job. It does not prove a
  live restart, which shows on the first bootstrap that upgrades Docker.
  A Portainer that has only just started may still read its environment as
  down for a moment, and the role runs the check straight after the restart,
  so `hcw-portainer-check` now asks again every 2 seconds for up to
  `portainer_check_environment_wait_seconds` (30) while the environment reads
  down. A refused token, a missing environment or an odd answer still fails at
  once, so a real outage is reported about half a minute later at most. Three
  new checks in `hcw-portainer-check.test.py` cover reading up inside the
  wait, still reading down when it ends, and a missing environment not being
  waited for; breaking each of those three ways turned the tests red.
- **The weekly supply-chain check no longer skips the image scan and the
  weekly issue in a week when a pin is behind (#1308)**. The check job's
  first step runs `lab-pins-upstream.mjs --summary`, which exits 1 when a pin
  is behind and 2 when a source could not be read, and records that code for
  the steps after it: the scan of the published lab images, and the issue
  that names what is due. A `run:` step with no `shell:` is `bash -e`, which
  the step's own `set -uo pipefail` does not turn off, so
  `node ...; code=$?` ended the step at the first non-zero exit, before the
  code was recorded, and every later step was skipped. Two earlier runs
  (13 and 14 October) failed this way, and so did the manual run after
  #1320; the step can only fail like that when the checker exits non-zero,
  and the 20 October run, which passed, found every pin current. Since the
  weekly run now moves pins through pull requests that wait to be merged, a
  pin is routinely behind when the check runs. The step is now `node ... || code=$?`. The test file that runs the
  workflow's steps now runs them with `bash -e`, as the runner does; the
  three new cases (exit 0, 1 and 2) fail on the old step, pass on the new
  one, and the old step put back is caught by the same mutation check as the
  others. The same run showed a second thing that would have kept the weekly
  output unusable: the host pull request it opened (#1324, which moves Coder
  to v2.38.1) failed `lab-pin-bumps.test.mjs`, because one test typed
  `v2.38.0` as the Coder pin it expected to find and so passed only while
  Coder stayed there. It now reads the pin from the real file, and passes
  with both the old pin and the new one.
- **The weekly lab supply-chain run now proposes tool and provider releases
  for the lab images, and no longer fails the whole week when cosign moves
  (#1308)**. Two gaps, both found by running the workflow's own steps
  against the live publishers. First, `lab-supply-chain.yml` ran only the
  `host` and `image-base` pin sets. The `image-tools` set (Terraform,
  kubeconform, Helm, kubectl, the Azure CLI and the Terraform providers in
  the mirror) was built in #1213 with its tests and its pull-request text,
  which says the weekly run found the newer versions, but no loop in the
  workflow named it, so those releases arrived only when someone ran the
  bumper by hand (azurerm 5.10.0 and Terraform 1.16.6 were waiting this
  week). It now runs. `image-base` and `image-tools` both edit
  `lab-image/versions.env` and the pull-request job applies one set's patch
  to a pristine checkout, so each of the two is planned from the pristine
  tree, held to its own paths, cut into its patch, and put back before the
  next one starts; the host set goes last because the Docker CLI fixture is
  recorded from its edits. Second, the cosign pin that #1240 added to
  `lab-host/bootstrap.sh` is edited by the host planner, but the host set
  did not list that file, and the workflow fails the run when the checkout
  changes outside every set's paths. Cosign had not released since, so
  nothing showed; cosign 3.1.4 is out now, and the next Tuesday run would
  have failed with no pull request for any set. The host set lists
  `lab-host/bootstrap.sh`, and its pull-request text says so. Because that
  is the script the owner runs as root on the lab host, the job that holds
  the App token now lets a patch change it only on its two cosign lines, and
  only to the shapes the bumper writes (digits and dots after
  `COSIGN_VERSION=`, exactly 64 lowercase hex characters after
  `COSIGN_SHA256=`, nothing after either, so a value cannot carry a
  command; CodeRabbit caught a first version that checked only how the line
  started): no other line, and no mode change, rename or binary hunk. An independent
  review of this change found the new per-set guard failed open if
  `git status` itself failed; it now writes to files with plain commands, as
  the existing guard does. Tests keep this from coming back.
  `lab-supply-chain-steps.test.mjs` takes the `run:` blocks out of the
  workflow and runs them in a temporary git repository, with stand-ins for
  the bump scripts, then checks the patches, the guards and the refusals
  (breaking the workflow eight different ways turned it red each time). The
  text test requires each loop over sets to list the sets it should, and
  every set the bumper plans except `image-digests`, which
  `publish-lab-image.yml` opens, to appear. A third reads the files the host
  planners edit from their source and requires each in the host set's paths;
  it is a text match, so it can miss an edit written another way. The weekly
  issue, the `--bump` documentation, the publish workflow's note and the
  tools set's pull-request text no longer describe the old two-set run, and
  that text no longer claims a checksum for the Azure CLI, whose pin holds a
  version only. The runbook, the lab host README and the lab image README
  now say the weekly run covers the tools.
- **The lab image's Terraform, Helm and azurerm pins move to their newest
  releases, and the tool bump's tests stop depending on today's pins
  (#1308)**. The weekly scan reports vulnerabilities in the Go code inside
  the tools and providers baked into the lab images. Terraform 1.16.5 to
  1.16.6 and Helm 4.3.0 to 4.3.1 are routine moves (Terraform's repository
  still pins Go 1.26.8 at that tag, which the scan lists as vulnerable, so
  they should not be expected to clear findings). The azurerm provider 5.9.0
  to 5.10.0 matters more: its repository pins Go 1.26.9 at that tag, the
  version the scan names as the fix for the standard-library findings in
  5.9.0. Each pin moved with the checksum read from its publisher by
  `node scripts/lab-pins-upstream.mjs --bump image-tools`, the set the
  weekly workflow does not run, so these releases would not have arrived on
  their own. Merging publishes the images; the next weekly scan, not this
  change, shows how many findings are gone. What the scan still lists for
  the alz, modtm and azapi providers, kubeconform, kubectl and the Azure
  CLI's bundled Python packages is already at the newest release of each,
  so it waits on those publishers. Two cases in `lab-pin-bumps.test.mjs`
  also invented a "newer" release (azurerm 5.10.0, Terraform 1.17.0) on top
  of the real `versions.env`, so each stops being newer the day the pin
  reaches it, and azurerm 5.10.0 failed them on this very bump. They now
  work the newer version out from the pin, and pass with the old pins and
  the new ones.
- **An evidence row can name the one requirement it counts toward, and the
  monthly audience rows do, so two audience months no longer read as
  community work or hands-on material (#1313)**. Readiness matched a row to
  a requirement by its source type alone, and the audience timer's rows are
  `manual`, which Docker Captain's `community` and `labs` requirements and
  Microsoft MVP's `reach` also accept. The timer's list named `reach` as the
  requirement each row is filed under, but the stored row never carried it,
  and the evidence validator refuses a key it does not know. Now an evidence
  row has an optional `requirementId`: `computeReadiness` counts a row that
  names one toward that requirement only (the requirement must still accept
  the row's source, so naming can narrow where a row counts and never widen
  it), and a row that names none counts as it always did. The timer stores
  `requirementId: 'reach'` on every row and may update it on a re-run; a
  month already stored without it is read once more so the rows get it, and
  a row the owner removed is left alone. The checklist on an application
  offers the same rows readiness counts (`evidenceCountsToward` in
  `ambassadorModel.js` mirrors the API's, with the same test cases). Docker
  Captain's `labs` accepts `manual` again, as revision 4 of its seed (the
  owner files hands-on material by hand); a stored seed that was never
  edited is brought up on the next read, and one the owner edited is left
  alone. Nothing to run: it takes effect with the next Functions and
  frontend deploys.
- **The AVM versions bot regenerates the image's record of what each pinned
  version calls, so its pull request arrives green (#1306, #1309)**.
  `AVM_CHILD_CALLS` in `lab-image/versions.env` is keyed by each builder
  module's version, and what a new release calls is only known once the
  image's vendor stage resolves it, so every bump the bot opened carried
  the record of the old versions: #1306 (`avm-ptn-alz` 0.22.0, the
  connectivity module 0.17.7, the spoke module 0.22.3) arrived with
  `scripts (operations)` red on "records nothing for avm-ptn-alz@0.22.0 in
  AVM_CHILD_CALLS" and the image's Build and smoke red in `vendor-avm.sh`,
  which the pull request body called by design. `update-avm-versions.mjs`
  now does what that body told the reviewer to do: after writing the pins
  it runs `docker build --target vendor --build-arg AVM_PRINT_PINS=1
  --progress=plain lab-image` (with `--no-cache-filter vendor`, since a
  cached stage prints nothing), echoing the build log to stderr, splices the
  `AVM_CHILD_MODULES` and `AVM_CHILD_CALLS` blocks it prints over the two in
  `versions.env` (no other line changes, and splicing twice is the same
  text), rewrites `LAB_IMAGE_CHILD_AVM` in `labImage.js` when the child
  list changed, and moves the exact pin on the module's block in the smoke
  payload (`smoke/terraform-validate-payload/main.tf`, whose `module "alz"`
  pins the builder's exact version on purpose and so broke on every bump of
  it). A build that fails, a print-out without the blocks, a line that is
  not the printed shape, or a record keyed by versions the file does not
  pin ends the run with exit code 1 and one sentence after the log, and no
  pull request opens. The workflow runs
  `scripts/lab-image-avm-vendoring.test.mjs` on the result before the
  upload, stages the two new paths by name (five, asserted by
  `avm-versions-workflow.test.mjs`), and the body says the record was
  regenerated. The vendoring test's own "goes red" cases carried the spoke
  module's pin as a literal (`0.22.2`), which would have failed the first
  bump of that module with a perfect record in hand; they read the pin now,
  as #1300 did for the frontend suites. Rehearsed against #1306's pins on a
  workstation with Docker: the vendor stage printed 17 children and 19 call
  lines, the splice changed exactly the 18 lines keyed by the three moved
  versions beside the six pin lines, and the vendoring test went from six
  failures to nine passed. `--children <log>` splices from a saved
  print-out for a run without Docker.

- **Study-guide refresher: an exam stored retired ahead of its day keeps its outline until the day**. The refresher and the outlines test judged liveness by the stored status, so the first green updater run after #1289 deleted PL-400's outline eleven days before its last exam day (#1291, closed). Both now ask `deriveStatus` for today, as the badge does; `eligibleCerts` lives in `scripts/study-guide-eligibility.mjs` with a unit test.

- **Learn-catalogue updater: a refresh no longer deletes `statusReadDate` and `availableDate`** (#1091's fields). The rebuild of every poster row carried an allowlist of fields that predated them, so each run erased them, PL-400 turned `retired` two weeks before its October 30 day and the data check refused the pull request (run 39218206063, after #1288). Both fields are carried now, with a unit test; a real run against Learn left only the sync date changed and the data tests green.

- **Learn-catalogue updater: two Node set-ups, because the two trees it installs pin two lines**. The Monday job failed on 2026-10-19 at `npm ci` in `frontend/` (`EBADENGINE`: the frontend has required Node 26.9 since the floors moved in #1161, `functions/` is pinned to the Node 24 line, both engine-strict). It now installs `functions/` under Node 24 and everything else under Node 26. The AVM updater's separate failure is #1287.

- **Cloudflare token roll: a child process that exits before reading its input no longer throws `EPIPE`** (`functions/src/lib/credentials/cloudflare-roll.js`). The spawn helper installs an `error` handler on stdin and writes with `end(input)`, so callers get the exit code and stderr through `close`; the tests model stdin as an emitter and add the `EPIPE` case. Found as an unlanded stash from #1247.

- **The lab host pre-pulls every template's workspace image, not `hcw-lab`'s
  alone (#1268)**. `lab_images` pulled one image into the Coder sandbox
  daemon, the digest `lab-host/coder/templates/hcw-lab/main.tf` pins. The
  guided-lab templates (`amo-guided-lab`, `na-guided-lab`) pin another, and
  name the local `default_image` rather than `image`, so their first
  workspace after any bootstrap pulled about 2.75 GB while the visitor
  waited. `files/lab-images.mjs` now reads the image of every template under
  `lab-host/coder/templates` (either local name) and plans each distinct
  digest onto the sandbox daemon; a template whose image it cannot read
  fails the plan rather than going unplanned. `scripts/lab-images.test.mjs`
  and `roles/lab_images/tests/lab-images-role.test.sh` hold every
  template's pinned image to the sandbox plan, reading the pins without the
  helper. The templates' digests are unchanged; the host holds two images
  until the guided labs move to `hcw-lab`'s.
- **Lab workspaces resolve names again, and the lab host proves it at every
  run and every 15 minutes (#1267)**. From the host firewall's first run on
  2026-10-17, every Coder workspace started its container and then never
  connected. Coder showed "Agent is taking longer than expected to connect",
  because the container could not resolve `coder.lab.hybridcloudworks.com`
  to download its agent. The Terraform docker provider (`kreuzwerker/docker`
  4.6.0) creates each workspace on the sandbox daemon's default bridge and
  then moves it to the workspace's own network. A container born on the
  default bridge gets systemd-resolved's upstream servers, not the stub, and
  keeps them. `dockerd` then asked them from the host's namespace as
  `hcw-coder-docker`, which `HCW-SANDBOX-OUT` refuses: at 23:20Z it had
  refused 576 packets since the 13:12Z boot, and its resolver rule had
  matched none. The
  firewall's README had said only a container on the default bridge,
  "which no template uses", would get those servers.
  - **The fix:** the sandbox daemon's `daemon.json` now sets `dns:
    ["10.0.2.3"]`, slirp4netns's forwarder, for every container. Its lookups
    reach the host stub, the one resolver the firewall allows, whichever
    network a container was created on. Every template is covered, with no
    template edit. After each start, `coder_sandbox` reads rootlesskit's
    API and refuses a forwarder that is anything else. On the host, the
    provider's create sequence with that nameserver resolved, fetched the
    agent, and booted all nine `hcw-lab` labs.
  - **The check that would have caught it:** a new `workspace_reach` role.
    It runs from `post_tasks` after `privilege_checks`, whatever the tags,
    so it follows every role and the handlers they notified, and a failure
    stops only the commit record. At every run, and every 15 minutes from
    `hcw-workspace-reach.timer`, it creates one container the way the
    provider creates a workspace, as the sandbox user, on the sandbox
    daemon, from the newest `hcw-lab` image there. From inside, the
    container resolves Coder's name, fetches 100 bytes of the agent and runs
    `git ls-remote` on the lab repository. A failure fails the run, naming
    the step, what curl or git said, and where to look. From the timer, it
    reaches `alert-lab-unit-failed` through `hcw-unit-failed@`, and it is
    skipped while the sandbox user does not linger (Coder off). A plain
    `docker run --network` resolved on the broken host, so the check copies
    the provider's creation order, and its test holds that order.
  - The `host_firewall` and `coder_sandbox` READMEs now describe the path
    as measured. The runbook gains "Workspace reach", which covers reading
    each failure and restarting a workspace that was stuck before the fix.
- **The lab host records the commit it converged from again**.
  `site.yml`'s `Record the commit this host converged from` runs only on a
  full run (`ansible_run_tags == ['all']`). On ansible-core 2.21,
  `ansible_run_tags` is a tuple, which never equals a list, so no run has
  written `/etc/hcw/applied-commit.json` since the upgrade. On 2026-10-17 it
  still named 2026-10-14's commit after two full runs, and the agent's
  heartbeat reported that commit. The condition now reads
  `ansible_run_tags | list == ['all']`. Run on ansible-core 2.21.4, it is
  true on a full run and false with `--tags` or `--skip-tags`, and
  `lab-host-site-tags.test.mjs` refuses the old comparison.
- **Coder's first-account check waits for Coder to answer (#954)**. The first
  bootstrap after #1246 recreated the Coder container with its new sign-in
  settings. It then asked `/api/v2/users/first` two seconds after the
  container started, before Coder was serving. The published port reset the
  connection, and the run stopped there (2026-10-17). `up --wait` returns
  once the container runs, not once Coder serves. The question is now asked
  until Coder answers 200 or 404, every 2 seconds for a full minute (31 attempts). A Coder that
  never answers still fails the run before its route is written. Run against
  a stand-in server that started six seconds late, it answered 200 on the
  fourth try.
- **Data-subject request runbook: supported commands, real estate names, and reproducible exercise record (#1237)**.
  The runbook (`docs/runbooks/data-subject-requests.md`) was corrected to eliminate
  fictional Azure CLI commands (`az cosmosdb sql query`/`document delete`) and non-existent
  resource names (`cosmos-hcw-prod-cus`, `sthcwprodbackupscus`). It now establishes:
  - Supported operational access: Web UI via the Admin Ambassador Hub with optimistic ETag
    concurrency, and an operational CLI tool (`scripts/data-subject-search.mjs`) querying
    Cosmos DB account `cosmos-site-prod-cus` and database `hcw` via `DefaultAzureCredential`.
  - Thorough search: Recursive inspection of all text fields across `ambassador` records
    and full enumeration of referenced files and images, providing Azure Storage CLI commands
    to delete matched blobs from `stsiteprodcus01` (container `speakerevents`).
  - Public submissions clarification: Confirms that public submissions in `content`
    (`functions/src/lib/submissions.js`) are completely anonymous and store no submitter
    or author email addresses.
  - Backup retention verification: Replaces fictional backup accounts with the real
    storage account `stsiteprodcus01`, container `cosmos-export`, and verifies lifecycle
    rule `expire-cosmos-export` (35-day deletion).
  - Verification exercise record: Replaces the unverified record with a verified,
    reproducible PASS using real commands and real estate assets.

- **Lab host: stale-bridge cleanup purges orphaned NAT rules for removed bridges (#1228)**.
  When rootless / userns-remap setups or dead Docker networks leave stale bridges,
  `hcw-docker-stale-bridges.py` removes the dead network bridge via `ip link delete`.
  However, Docker's default iptables rules in the `nat` table (such as
  `-A POSTROUTING -s <subnet> ! -o br-<id> -j MASQUERADE` and `DOCKER` chain jumps)
  remained behind in netfilter, matching unintended host-egress traffic and masquerading
  container-to-container connections as host gateway IPs. The script now inspects
  the IPv4 `nat` table (`iptables -w -t nat -S`) and removes all matching `POSTROUTING`
  and `DOCKER` rules referencing dead bridge interfaces by exact specification via
  `iptables -w -t nat -D <chain> <rule_spec>`, reporting `deleted_rules` alongside
  `deleted` bridges. The `docker` Ansible role triggers on either deleted bridges or
  deleted rules, and `privilege_checks` enforces the invariant that no IPv4 `nat`
  table rules reference nonexistent `br-*` interfaces.
