  Coder dump landed at 03:37:18Z on 2026-10-15.
  `alert-lab-backup-missing-vault` first opened at 06:30:23Z and stopped
  after the first Vault snapshot at 14:35:10Z. Read from Alerts Management
  on 2026-10-16, so the two-night backup stop the rows used to call for
  was not made. `alert-export-window-latency` keeps its design test, since
  a degraded export window cannot be staged.
- **Every log rule whose condition can clear now resolves itself (ADR 0022
  decision 6, amended)**. Four rules muted their repeats rather than
  resolving: `alert-logs-capacity`, `alert-lab-disk` and both
  `alert-lab-backup-missing` rules. A mute still opens an alert at every
  evaluation over the threshold and closes none, and on 2026-10-16 there
  were 43 such alerts open for conditions long gone. All four are now
  stateful: one alert per episode, resolved two clear evaluations later.
  The capacity rule's comment said its condition could not clear before the
  08:00 UTC reset, and that the reset left nothing to auto-resolve. That
  was wrong: the reset clears it. Stateless by reason, and so recorded:
  - the three daily rules, which Azure will not make stateful;
  - `alert-lab-unit-failed`, whose condition is a log line, not a state;
  - the Activity Log alerts, stateless by platform.
  The 205 alert instances open in both subscriptions were closed the same
  day, each with its reason. 137 had already resolved and 43 were stateless
  repeats of cleared conditions. The other 25 were security events, each
  traced to a fire test, a Terraform apply or the owner's own role change.
  Live after the owner's `hcw-azure` apply.
- **`alert-timer-overdue` is seen to fire: thirteen of fifteen alert rules
  are now on the Fire record (PLAT-4, #964)**. After the owner's apply put
  #1195's corrected query live (20:42Z on 2026-10-15),
  `Invoke-AlertFireTest.ps1 -Test timer-overdue` disabled `healthPulse` at
  20:48Z and the alert opened at 21:52:30Z naming it; the setting was put
  back as recorded. The runbook's Fire record row is dated. The two
  backup-missing rules remain, by the owner's call.
- **The Live Pages and Editor list truncation tests stand a bare element in
  for each row, so a loaded full run no longer times them out (#1194)**
  (AP-F6, #930). Both proved the 500-item banner by rendering 500 full rows
  in jsdom: 0.8 to 1.1 s alone and 2.5 to 3.8 s in a full `npx vitest run`,
  so other suites on the same machine pushed them past the 5 s default. The
  banner reads only how many records came back, so `LivePageRow` and the
  Editor list's `LiveItemRow` move unchanged into
  `pages/admin/livePages/LivePageRow.jsx` and
  `pages/admin/editor-list/LiveItemRow.jsx`, where the tests at the limit
  mock them; every other test in the two files renders the real row. The
  read, the count check and the banner are still the page's own: a test
  fails if the banner goes or its `>=` becomes `>`, and a new test at 499
  items in each file fails if it fires one short. They now take 65 to 117
  ms in four full runs, two of them with the functions suite running
  alongside. No timeout was raised.
- **No raw error text reaches a response body, and a repository-wide guard
  keeps it that way: follow-up to #1198 for #945** (AP-B10). #1198 converted
  fifteen modules and checked those fifteen files for one spelling,
  `(message|error): (error|err)?.message`; `error: error.message`, any other
  variable name, any other file and text passed through a helper all went
  unseen: run against c9536e03 (as against b23a7c73), the new guard finds
  197 sites, 37 of them raw text inside a response body (Cosmos, provider
  or socket text), where the old one passes.
  `functions/src/lib/http/error-response.js` is now the one door: an
  `AuthoredError` (and its subclasses: the CMS, settings,
  taxonomy, MCP, ElevenLabs, AI-router, GitHub-import, gallery-fetch, job
  payload-bound and rate-limit refusals) carries a sentence this code wrote,
  `authoredMessage` and `failureFields` show it and replace anything else
  with the route's safe sentence, and every failure answer carries a
  `correlationId` whose log line holds only the sentence, the error's
  content-free facts (class name, code, HTTP status, Cosmos substatus, the
  cause's code), up to three places in this repository's code where it was
  thrown (`at=src/lib/jobs.js:657`) and that id. The helper used to log the
  whole error; the message is not logged now, and of the stack only those
  locations. A caller's `x-correlation-id` is used only when it has the id
  shape, and the v4 worker's `traceParent` is read. The alerting runbook
  finds a reference's line in Log Analytics. Provider values that used to be
  relayed are now their status and machine code, each held to the door's
  code shape (`codeShaped`) before it goes into a sentence: Resend's error
  name, the OAuth `error` code and `token_type`, ElevenLabs's `detail.code`,
  the JSON-RPC code, a preview's content type, and the MCP sign-in
  metadata's addresses (scheme, host and a URL-character path only). A
  failed connection probe answers `{ ok, status, error }` and no upstream
  body; the provider's sentence on a rejected key stays on the super_admin
  API-keys page (#463). `no-raw-error-leaks.test.js` replaces the
  fifteen-file regex with a parse of every module under `functions/src`:
  `.message` or `.stack` off anything, a caught error stringified
  (`String(e)`, a template literal, `+`), a settled promise's `reason`,
  aliases and destructuring, scope-resolved by catch and `.catch()`
  parameter; a site is any object field, return, stored field or helper
  argument it lands in, a site inside a response builder's body (resolved
  by import, or an injected one called with a literal status) is marked,
  and an aliased `AuthoredError` subclass built from someone else's text is
  a site. A helper whose return holds a stored or log-only site carries its
  text to its callers, and that text is a site where it reaches a response
  body: the Podbean hub's reads and the Labs snapshot's lab checks were both
  that, and step 2 fixed them. Stored failures follow the same rule at the
  moment they are written: `storedFailure` and `recordedFailure` keep an
  authored sentence, or store the site's own sentence with the error's code
  and the reference of the content-free log line (`The job failed
  (ECONNRESET; reference <id>).`), still one string where a string was.
  That covers `job.error`, the Listen & Learn and podcast failure fields,
  the Podbean host record and the hub's reads of it, the cover, caption,
  inspection and Publer sync errors, the health pulse, the lab checks and
  the drift read, the Plaud token, the pricing and RSS job results, the
  Telegram activity log and the scheduled-publish records. The job workers'
  refusals and the study-guide, script, transcript, video, cover, grounding
  and Podbean failures are now `AuthoredError`s whose sentences name a
  status and the provider's code, never its words, so those pages still say
  what went wrong. Documents already stored keep the text they hold: nothing
  is migrated. The 149 remaining sites (none of them raw text in a response
  body) are listed in 146 entries, each with a class and a reason (100
  authored through the door, 42 that never reach a response, three `message`
  fields that are not an error's, and one stored diagnostic kept by
  decision: a provider's sentence on a rejected key, which #463 made the
  diagnosis and only the super_admin API-keys page reads), and the list
  fails on a new site, a stale entry and a wrong class. `getJob` now holds a
  job whose type is no longer registered at the enqueue floor (editor)
  instead of the viewer gate, and answers its 500 with a correlation id; the
  certification routes are pinned to refuse `_createdAt`, `_updatedAt`,
  `_etag` and `_ts`; a Forge Studio entry whose job write failed is said to
  be back in the queue only when the revert confirms it; and the admin
  client appends the `correlationId` to a failed call's message
  (`… (reference <id>)`) and keeps it on the thrown error.

- **Public reads return an allowlisted set of fields.** The article detail
  (`GET public/content/{slugOrId}`), the signed preview, the Listen & Learn
  certification read, the podcast list and the news feed each answer with a
  named list of fields, projected in the Cosmos query where the read is a
  query and filtered in code on every path, instead of a stored document
  with a denylist removed. A field a writer adds to a document is no longer
  public until it is listed. The lists are derived from what the public
  pages read (`PUBLIC_CONTENT_DETAIL_FIELDS`, `PUBLIC_PREVIEW_FIELDS`,
  `PUBLIC_LISTEN_AND_LEARN_EPISODE_FIELDS`,
  `PUBLIC_LISTEN_AND_LEARN_SET_FIELDS`, `PUBLIC_PODCAST_FIELDS`,
  `PUBLIC_FEED_CACHE_FIELDS` in `functions/src/lib/public-reads.js` and
  `public-preview.js`), and `public-reads.allowlist.test.js` pins each one
  against the frontend components that read it and fails when a response
  carries a key its list does not name. The article list keeps its existing
  projection, less the framework builder's three generation prompts (no
  public page renders them, and `useFrameworkData` no longer maps them), and
  now also filters in code; the snapshot read keeps its publish-time
  sanitizers.

- **Lab host: the nightly reboot asks at the hour, and reboots only an idle
  host (LAB-13, #959).** unattended-upgrades evaluated its logged-in check
  when the upgrade ran, about twenty-two hours before the 04:30 it then
  scheduled `shutdown -r` for with no further question, and nothing ever
  asked whether a visitor's lab job container was running; a job killed at
  the 04:30 reboot is the issue's evidence. The hardening role's override
  now sets `Automatic-Reboot` to false (the two settings read only while it
  is on are gone), and a new `hcw-reboot-when-idle.timer` (`*-*-*
  04:30:00` from `hardening_unattended_reboot_time`, `Persistent=false`, no
  jitter) runs `/usr/local/sbin/hcw-reboot-when-idle`, a root oneshot with
  the file system read-only to it, home hidden and the failure notifier in
  `OnFailure=`. It reboots only while `/var/run/reboot-required` exists,
  logind lists no login session (`loginctl`, class `user` or `user-` and a
  suffix; the `manager`, `manager-early` and `background` sessions of
  lingering service managers and cron do not count), the host daemon has
  no container with the agent's job label up (`hardening_reboot_job_label`,
  held to `JOB_LABEL` in `vps-agent/lib/docker-runner.js` by
  `scripts/lab-job-limits.test.mjs` and by the role's test; up is created,
  restarting, running or paused, so a job whose container exists and has
  not started counts), and the Coder sandbox daemon has no workspace
  container up (`coder.workspace_id` on `/run/hcw-coder-docker/docker.sock`,
  asked as root when the socket is there: a person working in a workspace
  has no logind session and the host daemon does not see it). It asks
  twice (CodeRabbit on #1191): when the first look finds the host idle it
  writes a maintenance hold, `/run/hcw-maintenance/reboot-hold`
  (`hardening_reboot_hold_path`, root's, 0644, in the service's
  `RuntimeDirectory=`), holding the epoch second it lapses (300 s on),
  waits for the labs agent to acknowledge it, and looks again. The agent
  reads the hold on every poll tick and claims nothing while it holds
  (`vps-agent/lib/maintenance-hold.js`; the claim loop moved from
  `index.js` to `lib/poll.js` so it has tests; `LABS_AGENT_MAINTENANCE_HOLD_PATH`
  from the new `labs_agent_maintenance_hold_path`, the same path, held
  together by `scripts/lab-job-limits.test.mjs`), caps any hold, unreadable
  ones included, at ten minutes from its write, and reads the time and the
  expiry from one descriptor, so a hold renamed over between two calls
  cannot pair one file's cap with the next file's expiry (CodeQL
  js/file-system-race). On a tick with no claim in flight and no job
  running it acknowledges the hold, writing its expiry exactly as read to
  `/run/hcw-labs-agent/maintenance-ack` (`labs_agent_maintenance_ack_path`,
  `hardening_reboot_ack_path`, `LABS_AGENT_MAINTENANCE_ACK_PATH`, one path),
  through a temporary file and a rename, in the agent unit's new
  `RuntimeDirectory=hcw-labs-agent`, which is not preserved, so a stopped
  agent leaves none behind; it withdraws it when a claim or a job appears,
  when the hold lifts, and when it stops. The script waits up to 45 s
  (`hardening_reboot_hold_settle_seconds`, at least a 20 s claim and one
  15 s poll tick) for an acknowledgement naming its own hold, asking first
  whether systemd calls the agent inactive or failed, when no wait is
  needed, and defers the night without one (CodeRabbit's second round on
  #1191: a fixed wait could not see a claim whose container was slow to
  appear). An agent that cannot acknowledge, an older or a stuck one, so
  costs a night's reboot and never a job, and the first `bootstrap.sh`,
  which enables the timer before it deploys the new agent, defers rather
  than risks one. The second look still asks logind and both daemons; the
  hold is removed on every way out but the reboot, where it stays until
  the reboot clears `/run`. One syslog line per outcome under the tag
  `hcw-reboot-when-idle`: the reboot and the deferrals at warning, which
  the Arc rule ships, and a deferral of a reboot pending 7 days or more
  (`hardening_reboot_overdue_days`) at err, with what to do, never a forced
  reboot; the days count from the first night a run saw the marker, kept
  beside the hold in `/run/hcw-maintenance/reboot-pending-since` (cleared
  with the marker by a reboot), because every upgrade that wants a reboot
  rewrites the marker's own time, and the held report ages its pending line
  from the same record; nothing pending at notice; an `apt-config`, a
  `loginctl` or a docker daemon that cannot answer, docker missing
  included, or a hold or record that cannot be written, is an err line and
  a failed run, so the notifier pages rather than the host guessing. A
  stop exits 143, which the unit counts as success (`SuccessExitStatus=143`),
  so neither an owner's `systemctl stop` nor the reboot's own stop job
  pages. It does not ask `users`: on the host that is rust-coreutils, which
  reads utmp, and systemd no longer writes utmp, so `users` and `who`
  printed nothing with an SSH session open (measured 2026-10-15).
  unattended-upgrade's WithUsers check read `users` too, so #1172's "no
  reboot with a user logged in" never deferred anything there. At most one
  reboot authority at a time: the role first cancels a `shutdown -r` that
  unattended-upgrades scheduled before the run (one its log names; any
  other scheduled reboot stops the run with what to do, because a root
  `shutdown -r` for the same minute is the same record; the cancel's
  read-back is keyed on the cancel having run, since check mode registers
  `rc` 0 for a command it skips), then installs, enables and reads the
  timer back active, writes the override that turns `Automatic-Reboot` off,
  and reads apt's effective `Automatic-Reboot` back, stopping if a later
  file turns it on again. The script stands down with a warning line while
  apt has `Automatic-Reboot` on, so a partial run or a rollback never has
  both rebooting; a run that cancels unattended-upgrades' reboot and then
  stops before the override leaves one night with neither, until
  unattended-upgrades schedules again or `bootstrap.sh` is re-run, and the
  runbook has the line that withdraws the timer and the three limits kept
  on purpose. The daily held report names the timer and its hour in its
  pending-reboot line, the role refuses a reboot hour that is not `HH:MM`
  and a hold outside its bounds, and `tests/hcw-reboot-when-idle.test.sh`
  runs the rendered script against stub `apt-config`, `loginctl` (the
  host's measured session listing among its fixtures), `docker` (both
  daemons, filtering on container state as docker does), `sleep` (the wait,
  where the agent acknowledges on a chosen second, with the wrong hold, or
  never, and where a job, a workspace or a login appears), `systemctl`
  (the agent's state) and `logger` in the `ansible-lint (lab-host)` job;
  `lib/poll.test.js` and `lib/maintenance-hold.test.js` hold the agent's
  side (an acknowledgement only under a hold with nothing in flight or
  running, written atomically, withdrawn when busy or lifted), and
  `scripts/lab-host-docker-proxy.test.mjs` the sandbox socket. The backup
  and Coder timer comments and the Vault pages that named "the
  unattended-upgrades reboot at 04:30" now name this timer, and the two
  Vault passages that said a reboot needs three unseal keys say that holds
  under Shamir keys only: this host auto-unseals, so its idle reboot comes
  back unsealed. `alert-lab-unit-failed` in the alerting runbook lists the
  idle reboot and the held report among the units that page. The timers'
  schedules are unchanged. On the host after the next `bootstrap.sh`; the
  runbook's two checks after it are `loginctl list-sessions` listing the
  login as class `user` and `shutdown --show` printing `No scheduled
  shutdown.`. Ask 2 of #959; asks 1 and 3 are their own changes.
- **A late podcast publish hook clears only its own job's reservation, under
  the version it read** (#942, follow-up to #1198). #1198 made the sweeper
  hand a poisoned or reaped job's `onComplete` the whole document, which made
  the podcast publish hook live on those paths; it already ran on `runJob`'s
  timeout. Running late, it read the transcript and wrote unconditionally,
  so it could clear a newer Publish's `host.podbean.pending` marker or erase
  an episode a racing worker had just stored, and a second job could then
  put the same episode on the feed. `recordHostJobFailure` now takes the
  job's id, writes only while the marker is pending and names that job, and
  writes with `ifMatch` on the `_etag` it read; a 412 is read again at most
  once, and a marker that has moved on is the answer. Reading whole job
  documents is cheap only while their payloads are bounded, and that bound
  now holds at every door: `newJobDoc` refuses a payload over its type's
  `maxPayloadBytes` (`JOB_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, 413), the Cosmos export
  scheduler and the Telegram /approve command, which wrote object literals,
  now build their documents with it, a Forge Studio entry whose document
  cannot be built is put back to queued, and `jobs.payload-bound.test.js`
  reads every `upsertDoc`/`createDoc` to the jobs container (by
  `JOBS_CONTAINER`, a `'jobs'` literal or a local name for it) and fails one
  whose document `newJobDoc` did not build. A payload over the bound is the
  caller's 413, not a 500: Listen & Learn's routes answer
  `JOB_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` with a fixed sentence, and the recording upload
  measures its job payload before it stores the audio, since a title within
  200 characters can JSON-escape past the 1024-byte bound. New
  `jobs.signal.test.js` keeps #1198's threading in place: it reads every
  module under `src/` that registers a job type (aliased and namespace
  imports included), pins the eight modules and the sixteen types, and fails
  a worker that never hands its signal to a call. Only an argument that
  carries the signal counts (the signal under any name, `ctx.signal`, or the
  whole context, so a thin wrapper passes); one that destructures it unused,
  only checks it first, names it in a string, or passes `Boolean(signal)` or
  `signal.aborted` does not. `noop` was the one worker that ignored it; its
  delay now ends with the job. And #942's own acceptance, that a timed-out
  job's side effects stop, now holds for writes: under #1198 a worker checks
  its signal at points it chooses, but its Cosmos and Blob writes went
  through shared clients that never saw it, so one that started after the
  deadline still landed (a timed-out Podbean publish rewrote the
  transcript's `host.podbean` after the job was recorded `timeout`). New
  `lib/job-context.js` runs the worker in the job's context, and
  `cosmos-client.js` and `blob-storage.js` refuse a write that starts there
  once the signal has fired, and check again before a read-modify-write's
  replace and its retry. A write already dispatched when the signal fires
  runs to completion, SDK retries included, and the job's signal is never
  handed to the SDK: cancelling it on the client would not recall it from
  the service, so the write could land while the job saw it fail, and the
  records that follow it would never be written. Each refusal is a fresh
  error with the job's reason as its `cause`. Routes,
  timers and the hooks run outside the context, and so does work that other
  callers join: the MCP OAuth token refresh, a process-wide single-flight,
  is started with `outsideJob`. A write that records something already done
  is kept past the deadline: usage rows (`ai_usage`), rotated MCP tokens
  (`mcp_servers`), and the version snapshot and audit row that follow a
  content write that has landed (`content_versions`, `admin_audit_logs`,
  `audits`), so a forge save cut off by the deadline still leaves its
  version and its audit row. `runJob` disarms the deadline as soon as the
  worker settles, so a worker that finished just inside it does not see its
  signal fire during the terminal write, and the publish hook now warns,
  without ids, when every attempt met a 412 and `pending` was left set.
- **Admin routes are the menu labels' slugs and page titles are the
  registry's labels, the single-draft RPC file says what it registers,
  deleting a live page archives it with ten seconds of Undo and the Archive
  board carries Restore and Delete permanently, and Ctrl-K opens a command
  palette over every admin page and the content search** (AP-F13, #937).
  `frontend/src/config/adminNav.js` is the one place a page's label, route
  and title come from: eight items routed to a slug that was not their
  label ("Publish" at `/admin/published`, "Review Queue" at `/admin/queue`,
  "Newsletter Hub" at `/admin/mailing-list`, "New Content" at
  `/admin/submit`, "Social Hub" at `/admin/social`, "Linkie Hub" at
  `/admin/linkie`, "Speaking" at `/admin/speaking-events`, "Platform
  Settings" at `/admin/platform`), and `adminNav.test.js` now holds every
  row to `/admin/<slug of its label>`. The old paths live on in
  `frontend/src/config/adminRedirects.jsx`, which also took over the five
  redirects `App.jsx` carried inline (#442, #569, #570) and, unlike them,
  carries the query, the hash and a nested segment through
  (`/admin/queue/<id>?source=content` still opens the review board);
  `adminRedirects.test.jsx` walks every entry and reads `App.jsx` for the
  route each lands on. Every link in `frontend/src`, the two e2e specs and
  the API's own admin links (`functions/src/lib/decision-center/links.js`,
  `calendar/collectors.js`, `cms/drafts-handlers.js`,
  `timers/newsletter-autobuild.js`, the ElevenLabs voice-picker URL) moved
  with them, since `itemLinks.test.js` holds the two sides equal.
  `components/admin/shared/PageHeader.jsx` (and `ServicePageHeader.jsx`,
  the Certifications page's) now render the registry label as the h1 and
  the document title; seven pages had written their own ("Content Queue",
  "Health Hub", "Integrations Hub", "Platform Settings Hub", "Speaking
  Events Hub", "Certifications Hub", "Ambassador Hub"), and
  `PageHeader.test.jsx` renders the header at every registry route and
  reads every admin page's source for a literal `title=`.
  `functions/src/functions/draft-http.js`, one letter from
  `drafts-http.js` and nothing to do with the Drafts stage, is
  `generate-article-draft-http.js`; the function name and route are
  unchanged. On Live Pages, Delete Live Page — one confirm, then
  `softDeleteLivePage`, which stamped a 24-hour soft delete nothing in the
  API ever swept — is Archive: `published → archived` through
  `transitionContentStatus`, which writes the audit row, and a toast with
  Undo for ten seconds (`pages/admin/livePages/useLivePageArchive.jsx`)
  that runs the new `archived → published` edge back.
  `lib/cms/content-status.js` gained that edge (publisher-only, like every
  edge into `published`; the port's "no resurrect-to-live" pin is reversed
  with the reason), and its archived and rejected appliers now also write
  the legacy `Status` word, because `public-reads.js` admits a document on
  `Status: 'Live'` as well as the flag — `public-reads.test.js` applies the
  archive patch to a document that says live every way it can and checks
  nothing serves it. Leaving the archive clears `archivedAt`; every
  non-rejected transition clears `softDeleteExpiresAt` beside
  `softDeletedAt`. The Editor's Archive board
  (`pages/admin/editor-list/ArchiveBoard.jsx`) carries Restore to live and
  Delete permanently (confirm, then `deleteContentItem`, the publisher RPC
  the Review Queue's delete uses; `cmsDeleteContent` is an editor-level
  hard delete and was left alone). MCP server removal keeps its confirm:
  the OAuth token lives only on the deleted document and is write-only, so
  nothing could restore it. `components/admin/CommandPalette.jsx`, mounted
  once in `AdminLayout.jsx`, opens on Ctrl-K, Cmd-K or its button as a
  Radix dialog — labelled, focus-trapped, Escape closes — listing the
  registry's pages filtered by what is typed and, from two characters, the
  content the list route's `search` matches (#1178; `lib/api.js`
  `listContentItems`), asked once per pause in typing and answered in
  order; Enter opens a page at its route or a content item in its editor.
  Every edge out of a page the public site serves is a publisher's:
  `lib/cms/content-update.js` gates on `published` or `isPublicDocument`,
  so a live `editing` page or a legacy `Status: 'Live'` one is covered, and
  a caller that names no role is refused rather than waved through (the
  Telegram bot's `/reject` names `super_admin`, its caller being the

  flows Archive replaced did, so `timers/publishing-watchdog.js` does not
  count an archived page overdue. The pre-render manifest's
  `PUBLISHED_PREDICATE` (`lib/public-content-manifest.js`) is now the
  public API's own `SQL_PUBLIC_CLAUSE` and `SQL_NOT_SOFT_DELETED` with
  archived, rejected and drafting excluded; its old three words admitted
  documents the API answers 404 for. `test/cosmos-predicate.js` evaluates
  it against documents. Live Pages offers Archive only on a published or
  rejected page, the statuses with an edge to `archived`, and says why on
  any other; the palette asks the content search only for 2 to 100 trimmed
  characters, the list route's bounds (#1184), and says so past 100.
  `transitionContentStatus` writes under the `_etag` of the read its gate
  and edge were decided from, and answers a lost race with a 409 ("The page
  changed since it was read; reload and try again.") and no audit row, so
  an editor's reject read before a publisher set a page live cannot land
  after it. Archiving a page also archives every linked legacy `blogs`
  document the site serves (`publishedBlogId`, `sourceContentId`,
  `publishedContentId`), stamped `archivedWithContentId`, and Undo or
  Restore to live brings back exactly those; `content-update.test.js`
  checks each with `isPublicDocument`. `deleteContentItem` deletes under
  the read's ETag (`deleteDocIfMatch`), refuses with a 409 a body's
  `expectedStatus` the document has left (the Archive board sends
  `archived`; the Review Queue and the framework review send none and keep
  their rules), and writes its own `content_deleted` row to `audits`, so
  the framework review's client audit row for the same delete is gone. The
  toast's Undo is sent once and disabled while in flight, and a restore on
  the Archive board re-reads the Editor's live list. The linked blogs are
  chosen from reads taken after the page's own write, each written under
  its read's `_etag`, and settled against the page as it then reads rather
  than the edge asked for: an archived page takes down every linked blog
  the site serves, a published one brings back the blogs it archived. Once
  a round's writes land the page is read again, and if it or a blog moved
  the round runs again (three at most), so a restore and an archive that
  cross leave the blogs agreeing with the page's final status; three
  interleavings are pinned in `content-update.test.js`. A blog deleted in
  between, or still contested after the third round, is named in the audit
  row (`linkedBlogIdsSkipped`, `linkedBlogsSettled: false`) and the
  transition still answers 200. `patchDoc`'s read-modify-write path
  (`lib/cosmos-client.js`) answers a document gone before its read with
  `code: 404`, as the patch path already did. `deleteContentItem`'s two
  failure lines are a fixed sentence and the error's code, with no
  document id. Rebased onto the role-cut menu (AP-F4, #928): Live Pages'
  Archive and the Archive board's Restore to live and Delete permanently
  sit behind the publisher `RoleGate`, and the command palette lists only
  the pages `visibleNavFor` gives the signed-in role and asks the content
  search only for a role the Editor is shown to.
- **alert-timer-overdue evaluates again, a KQL test refuses what silenced it,
  the weekly check reads every log rule's Resource Health, and the fire test
  matches the timer dimension** (PLAT-4, #964). The rule never evaluated from
  its create on 2026-10-10: its query took each timer's last due time from
  `bin_at(Now - Grace, period, anchor)`, Kusto requires `bin_at()`'s bin size
  and fixed point to be query constants, and `period` and `anchor` are columns
  of the rule's datatable. Every evaluation failed with `SEM0040 bin_at():
  failed to cast argument 2 to scalar constant`, the rule's Resource Health
  read `Unavailable / Semantic error` from 2026-10-10 22:55Z, and a fire test
  on 2026-10-15 stopped `healthPulse` for 95 minutes with no alert. Azure
  accepted the rule at create, and nothing in CI ran the KQL. The line is now
  `anchor + period * tolong((Now - Grace - anchor) / period)`, checked against
  `appi-site-prod-cus-01` for every timer due in the last day.
  `scripts/assert-expected-plan.mjs` declares the in-place update of the
  rule's `criteria[0].query`, its `before` read back from the live rule
  character for character, and a new test holds `overdueQuery()` to the
  heredoc in `infra/`. `scripts/kql-alert-columns.test.mjs` fails any rule
  that passes a per-row value where Kusto needs a constant: `bin_at()`'s bin
  size and fixed point, measured against the component (a `let`, `now()` or
  `toscalar()` is accepted; `bin()` and `floor()` take a column and are not
  checked). It failed on `timer_overdue` before the fix.
  `scripts/verify-alert-state.mjs` reads each live log search rule's Resource
  Health and fails `Unavailable` or `Degraded` as `UNHEALTHY`, naming Azure's
  title, and a read it could not make as `HEALTH UNREADABLE`, never `OK`.
  `Unknown` passes, as does a reason-less `Unavailable` on a rule evaluated
  less often than every 15 minutes, for which Microsoft reports no health.
  The report gains a Health column. *HCW Alert Rule Reader* gains the two
  `Microsoft.ResourceHealth/availabilityStatuses` reads. The owner writes the
  role and registers `Microsoft.ResourceHealth` in `sub-plat-mgmt-prod-cus`,
  unregistered there on 2026-10-15 (`docs/runbooks/alerting-and-support.md`,
  "Resource Health"); until both are done the run fails, naming each step.
  A refusal is never reported as an unregistered provider: that needs ARM's
  `MissingSubscriptionRegistration` code or the measured 409 `AuthError`. The
  runbook's rollout record reads the role's actions, both its assignments and
  the provider in both subscriptions, works in Windows PowerShell 5.1 as well
  as 7, and restores the previous action set from `0bd89190` (#1074).
  `Invoke-AlertFireTest.ps1` searched the whole serialized alert context for
  `healthPulse`, and every `condition.allOf[]` entry carries `searchQuery`,
  which names all 26 timers, so any timer's alert would have passed as
  healthPulse's. It now matches the values of
  `condition.allOf[].dimensions[]`, read at the live nesting
  (`context.context`) with a fallback one level up, and the Pester fixture
  takes the live shape, with a case where `searchQuery` names every timer and
  the dimension another. The Fire record stays "not yet" until the test is
  re-run after the apply.
- **Lab host: ansible-core installed hash-locked from the lab image's own
  pins, and the weekly pin bump moves it** (LAB-13, #959). The
  low-hanging-fruit entry below (#1178) says `lab-host/bootstrap.sh`
  hash-locked the `ansible-core` wheel. It did not: the script printed an
  `ANSIBLE_CORE_SHA256` it carried as a copy and installed with
  `uv tool install "ansible-core==2.21.4"`, which takes no hashes, so
  neither that wheel nor the eight it depends on was checked. The script
  now keeps no ansible-core pin. After it checks out the commit it will
  run, it reads `ANSIBLE_CORE_VERSION`, `ANSIBLE_CORE_SHA256` and
  `ANSIBLE_CORE_DEPS` from that commit's `lab-image/versions.env` as data,
  never sourcing the file, so an edit to it cannot run anything as root, and
  refuses any requirement line that is not one pinned, hashed wheel, so
  nothing in it reaches uv as an option. It writes the requirements file with the lab image fetch stage's
  own two `printf` lines, and installs it with `uv pip install
  --require-hashes --only-binary :all:`, then `uv pip check` and the fetch
  stage's count check, into a new venv under
  `/opt/uv/ansible-core-generations`, a directory of its own for every
  build, built beside the one in use. Only when that passes, and its
  `ansible-playbook --version` reports the pinned release on the pinned
  Python, does the link `/opt/uv/ansible-core` move to it, so a failed
  download, hash or check leaves the host on the environment it was using,
  even when that is a build of the same pins that has stopped passing; a
  generation is removed only after the link has moved off it, and one of
  other pins is kept until the next move. `ansible`, `ansible-playbook`, `ansible-galaxy`
  and `ansible-vault` are linked into `/usr/local/bin` through that link,
  and `hcw-vault-set` runs its Python through it. The old uv tool under
  `/opt/uv/tools` is removed after the play of the first run that has
  installed that helper, so a check run, a run narrowed with `--tags` or a
  failed play never leaves the helper on a removed interpreter; a rollback
  with `HCW_REPO_REF` to a `bootstrap.sh` from before this change removes
  the `ansible-playbook` link before handing over, so that script
  reinstalls its uv tool. The install commands, run in an Ubuntu 26.04
  container with uv 0.12.19 when first written, installed ansible-core
  2.21.4 and its eight dependencies on CPython 3.14.7, refused a wrong hash
  and an unlisted dependency, and installed nothing on a re-run;
  `hcw-vault-set`'s 81 checks passed with `/opt/uv/ansible-core` a link to
  a venv. `scripts/lab-host-bootstrap-ansible-core.test.mjs` runs the
  switch, the retirement and the handover against a stand-in uv, and holds
  the script to `versions.env` and to the Dockerfile's `printf` lines. The
  weekly `chore/lab-pins-image-base` pull request now also moves
  ansible-core to the newest release in its line that has a wheel PyPI has
  not yanked, with the wheel's SHA256 from PyPI's JSON API and every
  `ANSIBLE_CORE_DEPS` hash read back from PyPI, and moves a
  dependency only when the new release pins it exactly; a new line, a
  changed requirement or Requires-Python, or a hash PyPI does not serve is
  a note in the weekly issue instead (a dry run on 2026-10-15 proposes
  2.21.4 to 2.21.5). On the host after the next `bootstrap.sh`.
- **A Health view inside 30 seconds of the last one is served from the
  cache instead of running the eleven-query fan-out again, and a Platform
  settings save made from a page that is out of date is refused and reloaded
  instead of overwriting the newer save** (#946, the two acceptance items
  the merge of #1181 left open). The ops-health snapshot cache lived inside
  `createOpsHealthHandlers`, and `functions/src/functions/ops-health-http.js`
  builds a handler set per request, so every request found it empty; it is
  now held by `functions/src/lib/ops-health.js` for the worker's life
  (`resetOpsHealthCache()` for tests), keyed on the store and environment
  the snapshot is built from and not on the caller, since every admitted
  role gets the same snapshot and the guard still runs first. The HTTP file
  passes one module-level store. A build serves every view while it runs,
  however long Cosmos takes, and for 30 seconds after it settles; a failed
  build is dropped rather than served; and an alert update invalidates it as
  soon as the alert is patched, before the audit writes that can fail. The
  Health page's first read takes the cached snapshot, but its refresh after
  an action (Reviewer Digest, RSS Fetch, Run all, a probe, an alert answered)
  or a "Try again" sends `{ refresh: true }` (`useOpsSnapshot.js`) and gets a
  build that started after it, so the action shows at once on any worker:
  one starts at once when none is running, and refreshes arriving while one
  runs share the single build queued behind it. On the settings side, the
  `If-Match` branch #1181 added could not be reached from a browser:
  `lib/auth/cors.js` now allows `If-Match` (the allowlist is exactly
  Content-Type, Authorization, If-Match) and exposes `ETag` beside
  `WWW-Authenticate`; `GET cms/platform-settings/{setting}` returns the
  document's `etag` in the body and as an `ETag` header; and the Platform
  Settings tabs (`settingShared.jsx` `useSetting`) and the Mailing List's
  `NewsletterSettingsCard.jsx` send it back as `If-Match`, hold the one each
  save returns, and on a 412 or 428 say the setting was saved elsewhere and
  reload it. The precondition is now required: a save that names no version
  may only create the document (`createDoc`), a stored setting is replaced
  only by `replaceDocIfMatch` under the version named (412 `CONFLICT`
  otherwise, also when another write lands between the read and the
  replace), and replacing one without `If-Match`, or with `If-Match: *`,
  which names no version, is a 428 `PRECONDITION_REQUIRED`. Those two pages
  were the only callers of the write; no script, Telegram command, MCP tool
  or timer calls it. The reminders sheet keeps its merge under its own read
  (review of #910), so
  its read offers no `etag` and a timer stamp landing mid-edit is still
  merged rather than refused.
- **Alert fire record: twelve of fifteen rules seen to fire, and the SSH
  burst test writes lines rsyslog cannot fold** (PLAT-4, #964). The fire
  tests ran on 2026-10-15 from a detached runner (`Invoke-AlertFireTest.ps1`,
  one test at a time, every change put back and checked), and the Fire
  record in `docs/runbooks/alerting-and-support.md` carries a dated row for

  each line now carries its own port (`Invoke-AlertFireTest.ps1`, its Pester
  test and the runbook say why), and the re-run opened the alert in about

- **A lab job running when the host stops is interrupted and reported
  within seconds, not left `claimed` (LAB-13, #959)**. This replaces the
  210 s drain #1178 added: that drain then exited with the job's container
  still running and nothing reported, so the job sat `claimed` until its
  15-minute lease ran out. On SIGTERM the agent now aborts every running
  job: the runner kills the `docker run` child and starts removing the
  container by name through the agent's Docker proxy (`docker rm -f`, the
  one DELETE the proxy allows). Each job is reported at once, without
  waiting for that removal, which may take 10 s: `failed`, exit -1, with
  *The lab host was restarting and this job was interrupted. Submit it
  again.* The agent then waits up to `LABS_AGENT_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` for
  those reports (default 5000; anything but a positive whole number is
  the default), sends `offline`, and exits. Its `stopping` and `offline`
  heartbeats time out at 5 s each, and the timeout now covers the token
  request too. A claim already in flight is waited for within the same
  budget, and the job it brings back is reported without being started.
  The job loop moved from `vps-agent/index.js` into
  `vps-agent/lib/shutdown.js`, so the shutdown has tests. The `labs_agent`
  unit sets `KillMode=mixed`, so systemd signals the agent and never the
  `docker` CLI under it, and `TimeoutStopSec=30` (was 240). The new
  `labs_agent_shutdown_timeout_ms` is written to the env file and listed in
  `.env.example`. `scripts/lab-job-limits.test.mjs` checks that 30 s
  covers the 5 s budget plus both heartbeats, and that the env template
  renders every limit. `tests/hcw-labs-agent.service.test.sh` renders the
  unit and env file with the role's values in CI. The containers are the
  unit's to clean up, not the process's: a removal can take 10 s, longer
  than the 5 s window, and a crash removes nothing. The unit therefore runs
  the new `/usr/local/libexec/hcw-labjob-sweep` as root after the agent
  exits and before it starts, removing every container labelled
  `hcw.lab-job` through the daemon's own socket. It judges by what is left
  running, since the agent's own removal may still be at work, and fails
  only when a container is still running at its 20 s deadline. The proxy
  allowlist is unchanged, and `tests/hcw-labjob-sweep.test.sh` runs the sweep in CI
  against a stand-in for `docker`. On the host after the
  next `bootstrap.sh`. Two LAB-13 asks stay open on #959: reboot only when
  no job runs, and a hash-locked ansible-core.
- **The admin menu is cut to the signed-in role, the role is printed under
  the brand, and a control above that role says so before the round trip**
  (AP-F4, #928). Every item in `frontend/src/config/adminNav.js` carries a
  `minRole`, read from the role the server's guard asks for on the routes
  the page exists to call and recorded item by item in a table beside the
  registry (viewer: Dashboard and Health; publisher: Publish; editor: the
  other twenty-five); a row without one fails at module load, as the
  server's `requireRole` fails on a misspelt role. `visibleNavFor(role)`
  filters the groups and drops one left empty, and `AdminLayout.jsx` and
  the dashboard's Explore strip (`DashboardPage.jsx`) both read it, so a
  viewer no longer learns a page's role from its 403. `AdminAuthGuard.jsx`
  hands the role it verified down through `hooks/useAdminRole.jsx`, one
  value for the whole portal rather than a second status check per
  consumer, and the rail and the phone drawer print it as "Your role: …".
  `components/admin/RoleGate.jsx` wraps a control the signed-in role cannot
  use — `aria-disabled`, the click blocked, the reason as visible text the
  control names through `aria-describedby`, so it stays in the tab order
  and explains itself — and sits on the actions the server gates above the
  page's own role: Publish and Unpublish, Set slug, Re-host selected and
  Delete Live Page; Delete Rejected Now and Delete Permanently on the
  queue; Acknowledge, Resolve and Reopen on the Health alerts; the
  Recording Hub's transcript Approve, Return to draft and host Retry; the
  newsletter's Approve and schedule, Send test, Reschedule, Cancel send and
  Retry; Listen & Learn's Approve and publish; the calendar's Reschedule
  and Unschedule; and the dashboard's Recount (an editor write on the one
  page a viewer opens first). The server's guard is unchanged and still
  answers every request on its own; the gate is what the admin reads
  instead of the 403.
- **Polish defects that compound on a phone: no browser confirm dialog,
  toasts that stack and announce, a toaster that mounts with the admin
  shell, a loading state with a status role, one status request per user,
  and a catalogue failure that is shown** (AP-F12, #936). The three
  `window.confirm` calls that sat beside the shared modal
  (`frontend/src/components/admin/ai-engine/McpOAuth.jsx`,
  `components/admin/KeywordMatrixPanel.jsx`, `pages/admin/AIEnginePage.jsx`)
  and the Drafts page's navigation guard
  (`pages/admin/drafts/useUnsavedGuard.js`) are state rendered with
  `ConfirmModal` (ADR 0033 §2); the guard keeps the cancelled click and
  replays it on confirm, since `useBlocker` needs a data router the app does
  not mount, and `beforeunload` stays the browser's. `ConfirmModal` gained a
  `busy` state: the confirm button disabled under a progress label and the
  dialog not dismissable while the confirmed request runs, used wherever the
  action awaits one. `src/no-window-confirm.test.js` reads every source file
  under `src` so the dialog cannot return. `components/ui/use-toast.js`
  holds three toasts instead of one, each expiring on its own clock, and
  `toaster.jsx` no longer makes the viewport one atomic live region (every
  arrival re-announced the list and the toast it replaced was never
  announced); Radix's per-toast `role="status"` region announces each. The
  toaster is a static import of `pages/admin/AdminLayout.jsx` rather than a
  lazy Suspense child of `App.jsx`, so a toast fired before its chunk
  arrived cannot expire unseen; no public page fires one. A shared
  `components/ui/spinner.jsx` (`role="status"`, a label) replaces the bare
  `animate-spin` rings in `AdminAuthGuard.jsx`, `PublishedPage.jsx` and the
  two newsletter settings cards. `hooks/useAdminAuth.js` keeps one in-flight
  promise per user in its cache, shared by every mounted instance, dropped
  by `clearAdminStatusCache`, and never caches a failure; `lib/api.js` no
  longer forces a token refresh for `getCurrentAdminStatus` on every call —
  a page load takes MSAL's cached token, renewed when it has actually
  expired, and only an explicit re-check asks for a fresh one (`freshToken`),
  the case where a just-granted App Role matters. `AIEnginePage.jsx` shows
  a dismissible `role="alert"` notice when the model catalogue cannot be
  read, naming what still works and a Try again, where it used to log and
  show nothing.
- **AP-F11: the site's Content-Security-Policy drops `'unsafe-inline'` and
  the scheme-wide image grant and gains `base-uri`, `object-src` and
  `form-action`, the admin token cache moves to `sessionStorage`, and no

  `<style>` body in `style-src` and one per distinct `style` attribute
  value in `style-src-attr 'unsafe-hashes'`, computed from the pre-rendered

- **The drift monitor's Terraform row reads the last apply from HCP

  The row #1178 added to `scripts/check-deploy-drift.mjs` took the last

  and its `status-timestamps.applied-at` as the date, and counts the

  to the step, the way `tfc-plan-check.yml` receives it; its permissions

  `main`, a workspace that never applied, a listing whose newest run is not
  applied, every declared path existing on disk, and the workflow wiring.
- **Recording Hub saves again: the recordings create allowlist accepts the
  four fields both forms send, typed** (AP-B6, #941). #1181 put an allowlist

  `functions/src/lib/admin-integrations.js`) and left out `source`,
  `plaudId`, `recordedAt` and `status`, which the only two callers send on
  every save, so "route a Plaud recording" (`recordingCards.jsx`) and the

- **The content list's `search` is answered from the index, bounded, and
  reads both summary casings** (AP-F6, #930). The predicate #1178 added
  wrapped each field in `LOWER()`, which Cosmos DB documents as not using
  the index, so every search loaded all ~70k `content` documents across
  every partition. It is now `CONTAINS(field, @search, true)`, the
  case-insensitive form the index serves (a full index scan of the path's
  distinct values, not a full scan of the container), and the parameter is
  no longer lowercased. The term is bounded as `sort` and `limit` already
  were: `LIST_SEARCH_MIN_CHARS` (2) to `LIST_SEARCH_MAX_CHARS` (100),
  measured after trimming, outside which the list answers the same
  `{ error }` 400 an unknown sort field gets; a blank term is no search.
  `Summary`, the second casing the module header names, is searched beside
  `summary`, so a record whose summary lives only there can match.
  `cms-content.test.js` pins the clause, the parameter's casing, both
  bounds at their edges with a blank term and `q`, and a row whose summary
  lives only in `Summary`. No admin page sends `search` to the server yet:
  the Editor list and Live Pages still filter the 500 rows they fetch, so
  the bound has no UI mirror to add until the search moves server-side.
