- **PLAT-10 remainder: the Static Web App bandwidth comment reads the live
  DNS, the runner address is checked before it reaches a firewall argument
  and the storage window's flip can be measured, Cloudflare's ranges are
  held to the published list by a weekly pull request, the content account
  drops its localhost origin, the registration monitor names its real
  identity and what it counts, and the export window's effect on API latency
  is an alert rule** (PLAT-10, #970). `infra/frontend.tf` no longer says
  Cloudflare caching makes a bandwidth overage unlikely: the apex and www
  resolve straight to the Static Web App (read 2026-10-15), so every byte
  counts against the Free plan's 100 GB, and `alert-swa-bandwidth` is what
  watches the pace. `deploy-functions.yml` passes the address it learns from
  a third party through `scripts/assert-ipv4.mjs` (one dotted quad or the
  step fails naming what arrived) at all three places it is used, says what
  Microsoft documents about who writes the package on Flex Consumption, and
  leaves the host storage account's default action at Deny through the
  window when the repository variable `FUNCTIONS_STORAGE_OPEN_DEFAULT_ACTION`
  is the literal `false`, so one deploy measures whether the flip is still
  needed. `scripts/cloudflare-ranges.mjs` reads Cloudflare's published IPv4
  list, refuses a short or malformed answer, and rewrites the default of
  `cloudflare_ip_ranges`; `cloudflare-ranges.yml` runs it on Tuesdays and
  opens the `chore/cloudflare-ranges` pull request through the App, with the
  same recorded-paths guard as the lab pin sets (the set lives in
  `open-lab-pin-pr.mjs`; the pull request body says apply before the next
  deploy, because `assert-origin-lock.mjs` holds every deploy to the list).
  `infra/storage.tf` drops `http://localhost:5173` from the content
  account's CORS: nothing in the frontend fetches from that account by
  script, and the images and media it loads need no CORS.
  `monitor-functions-registered.yml` stops saying its identity can write
  site config (that split landed as #1098) and counts the host storage
  account's IP rules under that name, since storage IP rules carry no
  `ci-*` names. `alert-export-window-latency` (`infra/observability.tf`,
  severity 3, daily) compares the API's P95 inside the nightly Cosmos export
  window with the rest of the day and fires when the window is above 1 s and
  above twice the day's over at least 20 requests: ADR 0019's revisit
  trigger, measured, as a rule rather than the weekly readout the review
  asked for, because a readout from GitHub needs a workspace query grant the
  owner declined on 2026-10-11. The rule is a declared create in
  `assert-expected-plan.mjs` until the owner's apply, and has its rows in
  the alerting runbook and ADR 0019.
- **Completed low-hanging fruit remediations across Admin Portal, VPS agent, deployment drift, docs, and infra** (AP-F6 #930, LAB-13 #959, PLAT-3 #963, PLAT-9 #969, PLAT-10 #970).
  - **AP-F6 (#930)**: Added server-side `search` query parameter support in `functions/src/lib/cms-content.js` with Cosmos DB `CONTAINS`, added 500-item truncation notice and retry attempt state in `LivePagesPage.jsx`, and added unit tests in `LivePagesPage.test.jsx`.
  - **LAB-13 (#959)**: Extended VPS agent shutdown timeout to 210s (`LABS_AGENT_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS`) with active job terminal completion handling, added systemd `TimeoutStopSec=240` to `hcw-labs-agent.service.j2` and role defaults, and hash-locked `ansible-core` wheel SHA256 in `lab-host/bootstrap.sh`.
  - **PLAT-3 (#963)**: Added Terraform Infrastructure (`infra`, `cosmos-containers.json`, `tfc-plan-check.yml`) to deploy drift monitor (`scripts/check-deploy-drift.mjs`) and test suite.
  - **PLAT-9 (#969)**: Updated Azure Well-Architected assessment (`well-architected-assessment.md`) reflecting single Function App consolidation (ADR 0019) and verified recovery drill controls.
  - **PLAT-10 (#970)**: Corrected apex DNS direct routing comment in `infra/frontend.tf` regarding SWA 100 GB Free bandwidth limits, and added strict IPv4 format validation for runner IP lookup in CI deployment workflows.

- **Lab host: no reboot with a user logged in, the upgrade origins rendered
  by the role, and job containers with a stated swap bound and an open-files
  ceiling**
  (LAB-13, #959). The hardening role's unattended-upgrades override now
  clears and names the allowed origins itself
  (`hardening_unattended_allowed_origins`, Ubuntu's four) and sets
  `Automatic-Reboot-WithUsers` to false, with a test that renders it; the
  daily held-package report logs `a reboot is pending since <date> (<n>
  days)` at warning while the reboot waits, and the runbook names the
  owner's window (log out before 04:30, or reboot when convenient). The
  job runner writes `--memory-swap` as twice `--memory` (Docker's default,
  swap at most the memory limit, made explicit) and adds `--ulimit nofile`
  (`LABS_AGENT_JOB_NOFILE`, default 1024, also in the `labs_agent` role);
  both flags are sandbox-controlled, so a capability cannot set them. On
  the host after the next `bootstrap.sh`. The rest of LAB-13 (a terminal
  status for a job killed by a reboot, reboot only when no job runs, a
  hash-locked ansible-core) stays open on #959.
- **The Terraform busy guard fails closed** (PLAT-3, #963).
  `scripts/tfc-workspace-busy.mjs`, which `deploy-functions.yml` runs
  before any firewall window opens, used to pass with a note when
  `TFC_TOKEN` was absent, so from the outside a deploy log read the same
  whether the guard was off or the workspace was idle. It now refuses the
  deploy and names the secret to seed, and prints "armed" when it can
  read the workspace. `TFC_TOKEN` has been a repository secret since
  2026-10-08 (#980), so the deploy job already receives it. The runbook
  and the workflow comment say so.
- **`functions_scm_lock_enabled` defaults to `true`** (PLAT-10, #970).
  The workspace set it `true` on 2026-08-25, when the SCM window was proven
  under `Deny`, and the Function App's SCM default action read `Deny` again
  on 2026-10-14, so the code default now says what the estate does and the
  plan for the change is empty. The
  comments in `infra/variables.tf`, `deploy-functions.yml` and
  `scripts/assert-origin-lock.mjs`, and the required-inputs row, say so
  instead of describing the 2026-08-25 posture.
- **Version floors: the weekly pull request moves the `engines.node`
  ranges with the floors, and arrives green.** `update-version-floors.yml`
  used to move `scripts/version-floors.json` alone and open a pull request
  that was red by design, so every Node.js minor left five `engines.node`
  ranges for a person to move by hand (#1152). The updater now moves each
  range the new floors leave behind within its line, in its `package.json`
  and the root entry of the `package-lock.json` beside it, and re-reads the
  tree to list only what is still behind: an exact pin with a digest or
  checksum, a `runtime_version`, a `runs-on`, or anything on a new line.
  The commit job judges the patch before applying it, by a rule written in
  the workflow: the floors file, and otherwise only a `"node": "<range>"`
  line of a `package.json` or `package-lock.json`. The pull request body now
  follows `.github/pull_request_template.md`, and its first item says
  whether the floors check is the evidence or the work list.
  `scripts/version-floors.test.mjs` also fails a lockfile whose root
  `engines.node` differs from its `package.json`.

- **Lab host: a run can be narrowed to the roles that changed.** Every role
  in `lab-host/ansible/site.yml` carries its own name as a tag, so
  `bootstrap.sh --tags lab_images,coder` after a digests merge, or
  `--tags addons` after an add-on's digest moved, re-applies one area of a
  converged host instead of the whole play; the pre-flight checks and the
  privilege checks run whatever the tags. A narrowed run is not a
  convergence: neither `bootstrap.sh` nor the play records it as a completed
  run, so the site keeps saying the host is behind until the next full one.
  `ansible.posix.profile_tasks` prints the twenty slowest tasks after the
  recap, so a long run says where its minutes went. `lab-host/README.md`,
  "Running part of the play", has the tags and the two things a narrowed run
  is not. Owner ask 2026-10-14, after a run that took most of an hour to
  move three pins.
- **Lab host: the proxy check reports in plain words.** The privilege check
  used to print the three probes' raw answers, two of which the Docker CLI
  words as `Error response from daemon: … refused …` — the proxy doing its
  job, read as a fault. It now prints one sentence saying what passed; the
  raw answers appear only when the check fails.

### Fixed

- **Lab host: a host firewall for the lab sandbox, the container bridges and
  Coder's internal network (#954, #958)**. A new `host_firewall` role, run
  after `coder_sandbox`, adds the host's own `HCW-SANDBOX-OUT`,
  `HCW-BRIDGE-IN`, `HCW-CONTROL-OUT` and `HCW-REFUSE` chains, jumped to first
  above ufw's.
  - **The sandbox:** the sandbox daemon's user (the daemon and every
    workspace) may reach DNS on systemd-resolved's stub, TCP 443 on the
    host's own non-loopback addresses, and TCP 80/443 on public addresses.
    Host-local, private, link-local, multicast and reserved destinations,
    and all other traffic, are refused at once, and flows already open to
    them are cut when the rules first load.
  - **The bridges:** containers on `docker0` and `br-*` may open only TCP
    80/443 to the host.
  - **Coder's internal network:** the host's own new connections to it are
    refused; Coder reaches it across its own bridge.
  - **Loading:** `hcw-host-firewall` loads each family in one
    `iptables-restore --noflush` transaction and keeps each jump first and
    single. Both families are dry-run before either commits, a jump to an
    undeclared `HCW-*` chain is refused first, and a lock in `/run` keeps
    one run at a time. The play fails on any read-back difference, and check
    mode reports drift.
  - **Boot:** `hcw-host-firewall.service` re-applies the rules at boot, after
    ufw and before Docker, and reports a failure to `hcw-unit-failed@`. The
    sandbox user's manager requires it.
  - **Failing closed:** if a run cannot load the firewall, the sandbox
    keeps running only while the live rules exactly equal the last policy
    the role verified live (`/etc/hcw/firewall/verified`); otherwise its
    manager is stopped and the play fails.
  - **Removal:** `host_firewall_state: absent` removes it all in a safe order.
  - **Untouched:** ufw's rules and the add-ons' `DOCKER-USER` rules.
  - **Tests:** `roles/host_firewall/tests/hcw-host-firewall.test.sh` (real
    iptables in a scratch network namespace, 106 checks, in CI with ufw
    required) and `scripts/lab-host-host-firewall.test.mjs`.
- **No auto-delete on the owner's Ambassador hub (follow-up to #1234, SEC-4
  #973)**. #1234 set a 90-day container TTL on the `ambassador` Cosmos
  container, believing it held applicants' personal data. It holds the
  owner's own programs, applications and evidence, kept until deleted. A
  container TTL expires every document not written within the window, so it
  would have deleted the owner's records. The tfc-plan-check flagged it as
  undeclared before any run carrying it was confirmed, and it is taken off
  before any apply. `generate-cosmos-container-spec.test.mjs` now refuses a
  container TTL on the containers whose records are kept until deleted
  (`ambassador`, `content`, `content_versions`, `blogs`). The data-subject
  runbook keeps the hub in scope as a search of its free-text fields and
  files, redacting matches and keeping the records. Its `content` queries
  and its exercise record, which do not match the estate, are marked under
  review and unverified until #1237.
- **Lab host: Caddy's admin API moves to a Unix socket, and HTTP/3 is off
  (#958)**. The Caddyfile always renders a global block with
  `admin unix//run/caddy/admin.sock` instead of TCP `127.0.0.1:2019`, and
  `servers { protocols h1 h2 }`, so nothing listens on UDP 443 (ufw already
  dropped it). `caddy.service` creates `/run/caddy` as
  `RuntimeDirectory=caddy` (0700), and its `ExecReload` passes the socket as
  `--address`, which only the `caddy` user and root can open. The first run
  restarts Caddy before any reload, through handler order across the caddy,
  coder and addons roles, which a test holds; and a running Caddy without
  its socket is restarted. `caddy-adapt.test.sh` reads the admin listener
  and protocols back from the pinned Caddy, and
  `scripts/lab-host-caddy-admin.test.mjs` holds the unit, the socket path and
  the handler order. Runbook: "Caddy: reloading by hand".
- **`alert-kv-config-write` no longer fires when one of its own alerts is
  closed (#1216)**. An alert's state change is logged against its target, as
  `<vault id>/providers/Microsoft.AlertsManagement/alerts/<id>`. That sits
  beneath the vault, and the rule's only filters were category and status.
  So closing one of its alerts opened another and paged again: on
  2026-10-16 the alert cleanup closed three, and three new ones fired at
  01:37Z. Activity Log conditions have no "not equals", so the rule now
  names the providers that make real vault changes: KeyVault,
  Authorization, Resources (tags, which the fire test writes) and Insights
  (diagnostic settings). `Microsoft.AlertsManagement` is not among them.
  `scripts/activity-log-alert-filters.test.mjs` refuses any Administrative
  Activity Log alert without a provider or type filter, or one that lets
  `Microsoft.AlertsManagement` through. Live after the owner's `hcw-azure`
  apply.
- **The lab backup account's blob diagnostic setting no longer plans a
  change on every run (#1209)**. It set
  `log_analytics_destination_type = "Dedicated"`, which Azure keeps no
  value for on a storage target. Storage writes only to its own
  resource-specific tables, so the setting read back empty after its create
  on 2026-10-14, and every plan since proposed `"" -> "Dedicated"` again.
  The plan check named it as undeclared on #1207's merge run
  (`run-qrsPoBGgTrAZyqwa`). The attribute is gone. The rows land in
  `StorageBlobLogs` as before, as they always did for the site's four other
  storage settings, which never set it.
  `scripts/storage-diagnostic-settings.test.mjs` refuses the attribute on
  any diagnostic setting whose target is a storage account.
- **The `/education` page test computes its expectations on the day the page
  renders, not on the runner's real date** (#495, #1092). Since #495,
  `EducationIndexPage.test.jsx` has pinned the clock to 2026-09-10 in
  `beforeAll` but read `today` with `todayIso()` in the file body. Vitest
  runs a file's body while collecting it, before any hook, so the page
  rendered on 2026-09-10 while the expectations used the runner's own date.
  The two agreed only while no row's status differed between those days.
  AB-400 was the first row that did: `availableDate` 2026-10-16 and
  `statusReadDate` 2026-10-12 make it `upcoming` on the frozen day and
  `active` from 2026-10-16. From midnight UTC that day the Linux runners
  expected 49 bookable Azure exams and rendered 48, which failed
  `coverage (qlty)` on run 38834846071. The `frontend` row passed only
  because its path filter skipped its tests on that docs-only pull
  request. A machine on Central time still read 2026-10-15 and passed. `today` is now
  `todayIso(FROZEN_NOW)`, worked out from the frozen constant, and a new
  first test renders `useToday(earliestDataAsOf())`, the call the page
  makes, and requires it to return that same day. A clock mismatch now
  fails on the first day the two clocks differ, not on the day a status
  happens to change. The page needed no change: it reads one `useToday`
  and passes it everywhere. A local matrix of four collection-time clocks
  and six zones, UTC−12 to UTC+14, failed the old file in 19 of 24 cells;
  the new file passes all 24.
- **Monitor Functions Registered no longer fails on a storage window that a
  running deploy holds (#1205)**. On 2026-10-15 it read the host storage
  account at 22:45:38Z, while deploy run 38819173840 held its upload window
  (22:45:18Z to 22:47:35Z). It reported `Allow` and one IP rule as ❌, and
  the window then closed on time. Now an open window is believed only once
  no `deploy-functions.yml` run is in progress. While one is, the monitor
  reads the firewall again every 30 s for up to twenty minutes and passes
  as soon as the window closes. With none running, it reads again a minute
  later. An orphan stays ❌. A deploy still holding the window after the
  wait is ⚠️ and named, and so is one GitHub stops answering about for
  three polls. A Node crash is not taken for a deploy in progress.
  `scripts/check-functions-deploy-in-progress.mjs` answers the question,
  with a 15 s timeout and one retry. Its test runs the monitor's own step
  under `bash -e`, against a stubbed `az`, through that collision and the
  cases around it. The monitor does not join the deploy's concurrency
  group. There it would queue behind a deploy waiting on approval, and
  under the default queue a newer pending run cancels the older one.
- **Operator documentation drift** (PLAT-9, #969). `infra/README.md` said not
  to pre-build hub networking while `hub.tf` existed; the cost analysis
  called the Management budget "declared, not applied" after the apply had
  landed (read live 2026-10-14); ADR 0028 section 7 said host storage stays
  LRS when ADR 0031 (2026-09-14) chose GRS and Terraform sets it; and the
  lab host page's summary and identity rows still read "planned" for a
  host that has run since 2026-09-26. Each line is corrected with the read
  that corrects it, and a docs-build gate, `scripts/docs/check_stale_state.py`,
  fails the build on the stale phrases the review found an operator acting
  on ("State: planned", "not yet armed", "delivery is unproven").
- **The route error boundary recovers on navigation, and a failed sign-in
  shows its code** (AP-F7 #931, AP-F8 #932). One render error on any admin
  route kept the failure card on every admin route until a hard refresh,
  and always blamed stale build chunks; the boundary now resets when the
  path changes, tells a failed dynamic import from a runtime error in its
  copy, and shows the error message on admin routes. The sign-in callback
  page said "the browser console has the detail", which a phone cannot
  open; it now shows the Entra or MSAL error code with a Copy button that
  puts the code and the full message on the clipboard, while the message
  itself, which names the authority and client id, stays off the screen.
  `App.boundary.test.jsx` and `AuthCallbackPage.test.jsx` pin both.
- **Admin dashboard and Editor list say when a read failed** (AP-F5 #929,
  AP-F6 #930). The dashboard rendered "You're all caught up" over zero
  counts when the snapshot call failed, with a small red line beneath; it
  now shows an error state with Try again, and a later failed re-read
  keeps the last numbers with a "Numbers may be stale" badge and a Retry
  button beside the reason. The Editor list ignored its three reads'
  errors, so a 401 or a 5xx rendered as "No items match your filters"; it
  now shows the failure with Try again, which re-reads all three boards,
  and a board that comes back exactly at the server's 500-item limit
  carries a banner saying older items are not in the list or its search.
  `DashboardPage.test.jsx` and a new `EditorListPage.test.jsx` pin both.
- **The Publer proxy forwards only the paths and methods the Social Hub
  sends, and every write through either proxy leaves an audit row** (AP-B3,
  #938). `publerProxy` forwarded any verb to any Publer path with the
  server's key and no trail, so an editor session could reach accounts,
  members and workspace settings the Social Hub never touches.
  `integrations-http.js` now names its five endpoints and three methods
  (GET, POST, DELETE), and `rest-proxy.js` records every non-GET call,
  refused ones included, in `admin_audit_logs` with the actor, the path as
  sent and the outcome. `rest-proxy.test.js` sends every request the pages
  make and asserts an unlisted path is refused for every verb.
- **Landing zone HCL: the AWS and GCP emitters no longer hand state to
  generators that take none.** Eight calls in each of
  `frontend/src/lib/landingZone/hcl/aws/index.js` and `.../gcp/index.js`
  passed the normalised state to functions declared without a parameter,
  which CodeQL raised as sixteen `js/superfluous-trailing-arguments`
  alerts after #1157. The arguments are dropped; the emitted files are
  unchanged.
- **Lab host: the add-on secrets are read with the `vars` lookup.** The
  `addons` role built each add-on's secret environment with the `vars`
  dictionary, which ansible-core 2.21 warns about on every run and 2.24
  removes; it uses `lookup('vars', …)` now, so the run prints no deprecation
  warning and does not break on the next ansible-core.
- **Lab image: the pins the weekly scan could move (#1133).** The first
  scan the `check` job filed (2026-10-14) named fixable HIGH/CRITICAL
  findings in the images the host runs. Four of them have a publisher
  release to move to, and `lab-image/versions.env` moves them with the sums
  read as the file documents: terraform 1.16.4 → 1.16.5
  (`releases.hashicorp.com` SHA256SUMS), the azurerm provider 5.7.0 → 5.9.0
  and azapi 2.12.0 → 2.13.0 (the registry's `download/linux/amd64`
  `shasum`), and the Azure CLI 2.90.0 → 2.91.0 (published in both the
  `bookworm` suite the full target installs from and the `resolute` suite
  the sandbox template uses), which is the bundle that carried PyJWT 2.13.0,
  cryptography 48.0.1, msgpack, setuptools 70.3.0 and urllib3 2.7.0. The
  rest of the table — azurerm 4.81.0, alz 0.22.0, random 3.9.1, modtm
  0.4.0, time 0.14.2, kubeconform 0.8.0, helm 4.3.0, kubectl 1.37.1 — is
  already each publisher's newest release, so those Go-library findings
  have nothing to pin yet, and the Debian lines (openssl, libpcre2
  `~deb13u3`) arrive with the base digest the weekly bump moves. The
  `README`'s mirror line follows.

- **The lab agent's Docker proxy follows a daemon restart.** The proxy
  (`hcw-labs-agent-docker-proxy`, LAB-5) holds the daemon's socket as a
  bind-mounted file, so when a bootstrap run restarted the daemon under it
  — the 2026-10-14 run that took Docker Engine from 29.8.1 to 29.9.0 — it
  kept the old, unlinked socket inode: its own refusals still answered and
  every forwarded call got HAProxy's `503 Service Unavailable`, and the run
  ended at the privilege check. The `labs_agent` role now installs
  `/usr/local/libexec/hcw-docker-proxy-stale`, which compares the proxy's
  start with `docker.service`'s `ActiveEnterTimestamp`, restarts a proxy
  that predates the daemon's current start, and then requires `GET /_ping`
  through the proxy (`ansible.builtin.uri` on its Unix socket) to answer 200
  before the play goes on. The privilege
  check's failure message names the symptom. Tested against stand-ins for
  `systemctl` and `docker` in `ansible-lint (lab-host)`.

- **The lab supply-chain issue fits GitHub's body limit.** The weekly
  `check` job scans the two published lab images with Trivy and files its
  findings as one issue; on 2026-10-14 the full tables ran past the 65,536-
  character body limit (`Body is too long`, run 38493246343) and the week's
  findings were filed nowhere. The scan now writes JSON once per image, the
  full table (`trivy convert`) goes to the run summary as before, and the
  issue gets a compact per-package table — totals by severity, up to forty
  packages with installed and fixed versions and their first CVEs, a pointer
  to the run for the rest — behind a hard cut at 60,000 characters that
  names the run summary. `lab-pin-pr-workflows.test.mjs` pins the two
  renderings and the cut.

### Added

- **Lab host: an alert on an unexpected SSH login (#953, LAB-7)**.
  `alert-lab-ssh-login` (severity 1) pages when sshd accepts a login that is
  not `hcwadmin` by public key with the pinned key
  (`lab_ssh_admin_key_fingerprints`). Once the change that closes port 22
  sets `lab_ssh_loopback_only`, it also pages on any login that did not
  arrive through Arc SSH. It parses OpenSSH 10.2's `Accepted` line, drops
  VERBOSE's `Accepted key`/`Accepted certificate` follow-ups, and pages on a
  line it cannot parse. The rule is stateless and unmuted (ADR 0022 decision
  6): rows are chosen by ingestion time over 20 minutes and evaluated every
  15, inside a one-day window, so no login is missed (even one ingested late
  after an agent backlog) and one may mail twice. A test keeps the
  fingerprint variable equal to the key pinned in `group_vars`, and
  `Invoke-AlertFireTest.ps1 -Test lab-ssh-login` fires it.
- **Scanner triage: a CodeQL section** (SEC-5, #974). The triage standard
  covered Qlty, zizmor, checkov and Trivy but not CodeQL dismissals, of
  which 151 exist: 112 under the vendored harness, dismissed on 2026-08-21
  without per-alert notes, and 39 first-party. The section states the
  rule (every dismissal carries a one-line evidence note, the owner
  dismisses), records the harness dismissals as a class closed by the
  `codeql-config.yml` exclusion, and writes the evidence for the two
  first-party dismissals that have no note (#398, #388).
- **Lab host: the way back from the off-host backups (LAB-9, #955, PR 3).**
  `hcw-backup-restore`, installed by the `backups` role, lists the
  `host-backups` container as the Arc identity, fetches the newest or a
  named blob to `/var/backups/restore/` by a `.partial` name until the
  listed length has arrived, and with `--yes` restores a dump into
  `coder-postgres` (stop, drop and recreate, load, start) or a snapshot into
  Vault (`raft snapshot restore -force`, the token on stdin). The reinstall
  runbook's step 7 gains the restore as its last act and the **Last
  rehearsed / elapsed** line, "not yet" until the owner rehearses on a fresh
  VPS. Two corrections from the first seed on 2026-10-14: Vault 2.0 made
  `generate-root` need a token as well as the recovery keys
  (CVE-2026-5807), so "The root token" now carries the temporary
  `enable_unauthenticated_access` switch and its removal; and the encoded
  token is read from what the third key prints, since the attempt's status
  is cleared on completion. Tested with stand-in `curl`, `docker` and
  `vault`.
- **Lab host: the backups leave the VPS (LAB-9, #955, host side).** A new
  `backups` role, last in `lab-host/ansible/site.yml`, uploads the nightly
  Coder dump as it is written and a nightly Vault raft snapshot
  (`hcw-vault-backup.timer`, 03:45 UTC) to the `host-backups` container of
  `stlabhybridprodcus01`, as the Arc machine's identity: `hcw-arc-token`
  performs the agent's challenge, `hcw-backup-upload` puts one blob under
  `coder/` or `vault/` and logs one line tagged `hcw-backup-upload`, and no
  storage key is on the host. The snapshot token is the owner's one seed
  (`hcw-vault-backup-seed`: the owner's Vault token on stdin, a periodic
  orphan token under a snapshot-only policy, stored root-only), renewed by
  the unit itself; until it is seeded the unit is skipped, not failed. The
  role lists the container as the identity at every run and refuses the run
  when it cannot. The owner's line is in `docs/runbooks/labs-host.md`,
  "Off-host backups"; the restore and the rehearsal are the next pull
  request on #955. The seven creates #1147 declared in
  `scripts/assert-expected-plan.mjs` are removed, applied on 2026-10-14.
- **Lab host: where its backups go (LAB-9, #955; owner decision
  2026-10-14).** `infra/lab-hybrid-backups.tf`: a Standard GRS, Cool,
  Entra-only storage account in `rg-lab-hybrid-prod-cus` with one container,
  `host-backups`, under a 35-day time-based immutability policy — the host can
  write a backup and cannot delete or overwrite one inside the window — with
  versioning and 35-day soft delete behind it; the Arc machine identity's
  second grant, Storage Blob Data Contributor on that container only; blob
  read, write and delete logs to the Management workspace; and one alert per
  backup kind (`coder/`, `vault/`) when no blob was written in two days. The
  account name is an output for the host's `group_vars`. ADR 0032 gains the
  amendment of 2026-10-14, which also records the owner's choice over the VPS
  provider's object storage and local-only, and why uploads are not encrypted
  client-side. The host side (upload after the nightly dump, a nightly Vault
  raft snapshot, the restore helper) and the runbook's rehearsal line follow
  in their own pull requests once this has applied.

- **Lab pin bumps carry their dependents (#949).** Three files are held to
  the pins the weekly bumps move, and a bump that moved the pin alone failed
  its own pull request's checks on 2026-10-13 (#1122 `scripts (operations)`
  and `ansible-lint (lab-host)`, #1123 `frontend`). Now the host bump that
  moves Caddy also moves `CADDY_SHA512` in
  `lab-host/ansible/roles/caddy/tests/caddy-adapt.test.sh`, from the
  release's `caddy_<v>_checksums.txt`; the one that moves Docker Engine
  re-records `scripts/fixtures/docker-cli-agent-requests.json` with the
  pinned `docker-ce-cli`, installed into a temporary directory from Docker's
  apt index — the signing key refused unless it hashes to
  `docker_apt_key_checksum` (the value the docker role holds the host's
  keyring to), the InRelease verified against that key with gpgv, the index
  by the InRelease, the .deb by the SHA256 the index lists
  (`scripts/lab/record-docker-cli-fixture.mjs`, a step of
  `lab-supply-chain.yml` that exits with nothing written when the fixture
  already matches); and the image-base bump rewrites the base tag and
  CPython release the Docker guide page names
  (`frontend/src/pages/docker/BuildingImagesPage.jsx`), and sets that page's
  `CHECKED_ON` to the day of the bump, since the pull request's `frontend`
  check is the read of the page against those files. The three files join
  their set's paths in `open-lab-pin-pr.mjs`, whose pull request body now
  carries the template's sections in order with only the true boxes ticked
  (CodeRabbit's Description check warned on #1122 without them). The tests that named those
  values by hand — `lab-pin-bumps.test.mjs` against the live `group_vars`,
  `DockerGuides.test.jsx` against `python:3.14.7-slim-trixie` — read them
  from the files instead, so a bump pull request is green on its own and a
  merged bump does not break `main`.

- **Recording Hub: a Stats tab with the show's Podbean statistics.** Closes
  #1115 (the second of two slices; the first added the Distribution tab's
  live status and downloads). The show's figures lived only on Podbean's
  site; the hub now reads them through the same client (ADR 0029 §1c).
  - **`GET cms/podcast/host/stats?range=30d|90d|12m`** (`editor`;
    `lib/podcast/host-stats.js`): six independent Podbean reads over the
    range's window — downloads by day (`30d`, `90d`, `period: 'd'`) or by
    month (`12m`, `period: 'm'`, from the first of the month eleven months
    ago), countries, platforms, sources, monthly listener retention and the
    audience counts (`followers`, `likes`, `comments`,
    `totalEpisodeLengthSeconds`). A failed sub-read is `null` in its place
    with its recorded error under `errors.<name>`; the others still answer
    and the response is 200. A range not offered is 400 before any read.
    Cached 60 minutes per range in `admin_config/podbean_host_stats_<range>`;
    `?refresh=1` reads live except while the range's cache is under a minute
    old, and the document carries the client's `accountKey`, both as the
    overview does. Not configured is 200 `{ configured: false, range, reason }`
    with no call.
  - **`lib/podcast/host-cache.js`**: the read-through `admin_config` cache
    the overview and the statistics now share — served while younger than
    the TTL; on refresh, served while younger than the floor (read from the
    shared document, so every session and instance together make one live
    read a minute); a miss for any other Podbean account; written create-only
    first and etag-conditionally after; logged by error code and never a
    dependency when it cannot be read or written. `host-reads.js` moved onto
    it with no change in behaviour.
  - **Stats tab** (`?tab=stats`; `statistics`, `downloads`, `analytics` and
    `listeners` land there): a 30 days / 90 days / 12 months picker, the
    total downloads and a bar chart with one bar per day or month (zero where
    nothing was reported, so a quiet day is a bar and not a gap), top
    countries (named), platforms and sources as ranked lists with share %
    and an `Other` row past eight, retention as a small table with each
    point as a percentage, and the audience counts as tiles. Loading,
    not-configured, failed-read, per-section failure and "no data yet"
    states each say so. The chart is recharts, as AI Engine → Usage uses.
  - **Two documented-but-unmeasured shapes are taken either way**: a monthly
    download key of `YYYY-MM` is a month and `YYYY-MM-DD` folds into its
    month; a `retention` value at or under 1 is a fraction and above 1 a
    percentage. Both are stated in `statsView.js` and pinned by its tests,
    so the first live reading has a test to correct.
  - Contract and inventory: `.azure/api-surface.json`,
    `functions/function-inventory.json` (`getPodcastHostStats`).

- **Recording Hub: Podbean's live status and downloads per published
  episode.** Part of #1115, re-scoped 2026-10-13 after Podbean's MCP server
  was measured unusable from a web app (redirect allowlist; a developer-app
  token gets 401 at `/mcp`). The Distribution tab showed only what the
  publish job recorded; it now reads Podbean through the client the publish
  already authenticates with (ADR 0029 §1c).
  - **`podbean.js` gains the reads**: `getEpisode`, `getDownloadStats`,
    `getCountryStats`, `getPlatformStats`, `getSourceStats`,
    `getUserRetention` and `getAnalyticReports`, every one a `GET` through the
    same `call()` with the token as `access_token`. Dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`, a
    real day, start on or before end) and periods (`d|m`, `m|w`) are refused
    as `VALIDATION` before any request. `types[]` is sent as a repeated
    parameter; the shapes are Podbean's documented ones and none is measured
    live yet — the client tests pin the documented requests.
  - **`GET cms/podcast/host/overview`** (`editor`; `lib/podcast/host-reads.js`):
    every transcript whose `host.podbean.episodeId` is set, joined by id to
    one page of the show's newest 100 episodes, plus the listed episodes no
    transcript names (`transcriptId: null` — the three published by hand).
    Per episode: Podbean's title, status, permalink, publish time, and the
    last 30 days of downloads (`{ total, byDay }`), newest first and at most
    20 statistics reads per overview (`downloadsCapped` counts the rest). A
    Podbean failure lands where it happened — `errors.show`,
    `errors.episodes` (then on every transcript row, and no statistics are
    read), or `error` on one row — in the publish job's recorded-error shape,
    and the answer is still 200. Cached 15 minutes in
    `admin_config/podbean_host_overview`; `?refresh=1` reads live, except
    while the cache is under a minute old, so every editor session, tab and
    instance together make at most one live read a minute against the
    bucket publishing shares (the floor is read from the shared document).
    The cached document carries the client's `accountKey` (sixteen hex
    digits of SHA-256 over the client id, never the id), so settings pointed
    at another Podbean account make it a miss rather than serving the
    previous account's rows until expiry. A cache that cannot be read or
    written is logged content-free and the live overview is served. Not
    configured is 200 `{ configured: false, reason }` with no call. Logs
    carry counts and codes, never a title or the token.
  - **Distribution tab**: under each "Published to Podbean" record, a Podbean
    line with the live status badge (Live / Draft on Podbean), the episode
    page, "N downloads, last 30 days" and a 30-bar sparkline; an "Also on
    Podbean" group for the episodes this hub never sent; a "Podbean read
    <when> (cached)" status line with Refresh. Loading, not-configured and
    failed-read states each say so; a failed read shows no stale counts. The
    overview is read when the tab first mounts, not on page load.
  - Contract and inventory: `.azure/api-surface.json`,
    `functions/function-inventory.json` (`getPodcastHostOverview`).

- **MCP Disconnect revokes the grant at the provider (RFC 7009).** Closes
  #1116, raised by CodeRabbit on #1114. Disconnect on an OAuth MCP server
  deleted the stored token pair and left the grant live at the provider
  until its refresh token expired or the owner revoked it there.
  - **Discovery keeps the `revocation_endpoint`** the authorization-server
    metadata names (RFC 8414), https only, on the pending sign-in and then on
    the stored connection (`oauth.revocationEndpoint`), beside the token
    endpoint — so, like the token endpoint, it is set only by the flow and
    never by a config write. A missing or non-https one is stored as none;
    it is not a reason to refuse the sign-in. Podbean advertises
    `https://mcp.podbean.com/revoke` (read 2026-10-13); Replicate and
    Hostinger did not when read.
  - **Disconnect revokes first, then deletes.** The refresh token, then the
    access token, each POSTed as `token` + `token_type_hint` with the client
    authentication the registration chose (client id in the form for a public
    client; Basic or in the body for a confidential one), through the same
    guarded request as every token call: https only, no redirects, one
    deadline. The local delete happens whatever the provider answers, so an
    outage cannot keep a token on this side. The response carries `revoked`
    (`true`, `false` with a short `reason`, or `null` when there is nowhere
    to revoke) and `issuer`; the audit row records both. No token reaches a
    log or the response.
  - **The card says which.** "Disconnected and revoked at mcp.podbean.com",
    or "Disconnected here; the grant may still be live at mcp.podbean.com —
    revoke it in your mcp.podbean.com account". A provider without a
    revocation endpoint gets the plain "disconnected" toast as before. The
    Podbean card's notes and the Connect runbook say the same.

- **Podbean's MCP server in the AI Engine (Admin → AI Engine → MCP
  Servers).** The show moved to Podbean on 2026-10-13, and Podbean runs a
  hosted MCP server at `https://mcp.podbean.com/mcp`. It covers the show's
  episodes, its details and its listener statistics.
  - **Sign-in:** read that day, the server advertises RFC 9728 and RFC 8414
    discovery, PKCE (`S256`), `none` client authentication and a
    `registration_endpoint`. So the existing Connect flow signs in with no key:
    press Connect, sign in at Podbean, approve. The token is kept server-side
    and renewed by the MCP token timer, like Hostinger's and Replicate's.
  - **Ships switched off.** Its tools can publish, edit and permanently delete
    episodes.
  - **Where it is recorded:** `seed.js` seeds it (the AI Engine page adds a
    missing default on load). The card treats it as built-in. The credentials
    register lists its OAuth token as `mcp-podbean`. The tests pin it among the
    Connect servers.

- **`podcast.hybridcloudworks.com` for the show's Podbean website.**
  Hybrid Cloud Insights moved from RSS.com to Podbean on 2026-10-13.
  - **The feed:** it is now `https://feed.podbean.com/hybridcloudinsights/feed.xml`. RSS.com's feed and Podbean's first address (`spatino`) both answer 301 towards it, and all three episodes keep their GUIDs.
  - **The record:** `cloudflare_dns_record.podcast_podbean` points `podcast` at `pbcdn2.podbean.com`, DNS-only like `docs`, because Podbean issues the certificate itself.
  - **Why a subdomain:** Podbean's "Use a domain I own" page prefills `www`, which is the site. The comment in `infra/frontend.tf` and the edge DNS runbook say so, so the podcast never takes `www` or the apex.
  - The plan checker declares the one create.

  - The 2026-08 review's T-713 "FIXED" counted only the storage account's

- **Ambassador hub: AWS Community Builders, GitKraken's real quarterly
  rule, and what keeps a membership active (owner request 2026-10-11).**
  - **AWS Community Builders** joins the seeded catalogue, from its program
    page:
    - the waitlist link;
    - open to every AWS builder, with a limited intake each year;
    - the yearly January cycle, noted as "edit to match".
  - **GitKraken Ambassador** takes its rule from the program's quarterly
    check-in of 2026-10-08:
    - Two or more content pieces a quarter, each logged on the program's
      contribution tracker, on that quarter's tab.
    - Its criteria are the check-in's focus: review sites, Reddit, articles
      that use data, shared GitKraken content, and videos on Merge
      Conflicts, Dev AI Use and Commit Graph.
    - The stored program updates itself on the next read, field by field,
      wherever it still holds the first seed's guess
      (`SUPERSEDED_SEED_VALUES`). A field the owner edited stays as it is.
  - **Upkeep** (`upkeep`): a program can say what keeps a held membership
    active, as a minimum of evidence filed under it in every calendar
    quarter or year. A card whose membership is Active shows this period's
    count and its due date, and Details shows this period and the last. Only
    evidence filed under the program counts; general evidence says nothing
    about it.
  - **Contribution tracker** (`contributionTrackerUrl`): the link to where a
    program wants contributions logged. It is set on Settings and stored
    with the program only. No seed carries one, and a test holds the seed
    file free of shared-document links: such a link is private to a
    program's members, and this repository is public.

- **Alerting: one script runs each PLAT-4 fire test and proves the alert
  fired from Azure Monitor, not the inbox (#964).** "Making each one fire
  once" in `docs/runbooks/alerting-and-support.md` was ten long manual blocks
  whose proof was a mail arriving. `scripts/alerts/Invoke-AlertFireTest.ps1
  -Test <name>` runs one block as written and puts it back.
  - Same stop conditions, refusing and changing nothing when one fails; the
    same record files in the home folder (`plat4-rbac-test.json`,
    `plat4-roledef-test.json`, `plat4-poison-test.json`, `plat4-swa-test.json`,
    `plat4-timer-test.json`), written before the change they describe, with
    `Out-File -NoClobber` where the runbook makes the record the lock. Every
    change is put back in a `finally`, so a failure or Ctrl+C part-way still
    restores, and a record is removed only once the runbook's own read shows
    nothing left; otherwise it is kept and the run exits 3. `-Recover` does a
    test's recovery from its record; `-WhatIf` runs the reads and prints every
    change as the one line it would run.
  - The proof is Alerts - Get All (`Microsoft.AlertsManagement/alerts`,
    api-version 2019-03-01, the version Microsoft's reference documents),
    filtered to the rule's id over the last hour and read once a minute.
    `PASS <rule> fired at <time>` needs an alert that started after the test
    did; `alert-timer-overdue`'s must also name `healthPulse` in its context.
    Anything else is `FAIL <rule>: no alert within <n> minutes` and exit 2.
    The run ends with the Fire record rows to paste.
  - Checks the runbook leaves implicit, each a read: az's default
    subscription is `sub-app-site-prod-cus`; every rule exists before
    anything changes; `swa-bandwidth` saves nothing unless the threshold reads
    2666666666; `lab-agent-offline` refuses unless
    `FEATURE_FLAG_CHECK_AGENT_HEALTH` is `true`.
  - `scripts/alerts/Invoke-AlertFireTest.Tests.ps1` (Pester 5) tests the
    parser, every stop condition, the lock, `-WhatIf`, and each put-back when
    the action fails, against a mocked az, and runs the whole script against
    a stand-in az that refuses every write. Repository Policy's Pester step
    now runs `scripts/alerts`. The runbook's section opens with a table of
    the ten run lines and the seven recovery lines.

- **Hybrid Lab: an hourly canary runs one real lab job end to end, and a
  refused Coder status token is raised (#1009, "PR 2: prevent recurrence",
  items 2 and 4).** The admin Labs probe enqueues and cancels, so it passed
  with no agent at all while no lab job ran for days; and Coder refused the
  status token for about 32 hours with only a card saying "unknown".
  - `labCanary` (`functions/src/lib/labs/canary.js`), hourly at 20 past,
    behind `FEATURE_FLAG_LAB_CANARY` (`LAB_CANARY` in `enabled_timers`, off
    until the owner arms it): one `shell-echo` job with the payload
    `hcw-canary <job id>`, enqueued as `enqueueLabJob` writes one, waited for
    up to 150 s, passed only when the agent echoes the payload exactly, then
    deleted under its ETag. Nothing is enqueued when no active agent
    registered for `shell-echo` is online. A job still queued at the
    deadline is cancelled and deleted; one still claimed is left to finish,
    and the next run deletes it (or withdraws it past the claim lease) and
    enqueues nothing new meanwhile. Each run is recorded with its claim and
    run times in `admin_config/lab_canary`, where the job's id is reserved
    under the record's ETag before the job is created, so a run that dies
    or cannot write its record never loses a job to the next. The record
    also names its owning run (`activeRun`), so an overlapping run touches
    nothing and a run's last write never clears another's reservation.
  - Every read of Coder with `CODER-STATUS-TOKEN` records Coder's answer in
    `admin_config/coder_status_token` (`recordTokenAnswer`, ETag-guarded,
    an unchanged answer at most hourly, one outage keeping its start), kept
    per operation: the labs status read and the Integrations card's read of
    the token's own record, so a refusal is cleared only by the same read
    succeeding. A 401 writes a warning starting `coder-status: Coder
    refused CODER_STATUS_TOKEN (401)` for a log alert to match; a 403 now
    says it lacks a read scope rather than "expired or revoked".
    `checkAgentHealth`, which is armed, runs `checkTokenIfDue` and so asks
    Coder directly once an hour, never through the anonymous minute cache,
    whether or not the canary is armed, so warm-cache traffic cannot hide a
    refusal; visitors' live reads record their answers too.
  - Two more Health Hub probes, recorded by the pulse and shown by the Labs
    snapshot: **Lab job canary** (`lab-canary`; offline when nothing ran the
    job, critical when it ran and failed, unknown once the canary stops) and
    **Coder status token** (`coder-token`; critical from the first refusal
    until Coder accepts it again, unknown after a day without a read).
  - The timer is in `local.timer_catalogue`, the `enabled_timers` validation,
    `function-inventory.json` and `alert-timer-overdue`'s schedule map; the
    plan check declares the new flag, its arming, and the rule's query with
    the extra row (rendered with `terraform console` and checked against the
    map by a test). No alert rule is added; the alerting runbook lists the
    two queries a follow-up rule would use.

- **Hybrid Lab: the site raises a host that lags `main`, and a Coder
  template the host did not publish (#1009, "PR 2: prevent recurrence";
  the heartbeat half of LAB-4, #950).** On 2026-10-08 the host was six
  merged pull requests behind and nothing said so. It raises; nothing here
  re-runs the playbook.
  - The host records what it converged from. `site.yml`'s last task, after
    every role, handler and privilege check, writes
    `/etc/hcw/applied-commit.json` (`root:root` `0644`; the commit, its
    committer date, the time the run finished;
    `lab_host_applied_commit_file`). A failed run leaves the previous
    record and a `--check` run writes nothing.
  - The agent reads it on every heartbeat (`vps-agent/lib/applied-commit.js`)
    and sends it as `applied`; `heartbeatAgent` checks it (a full sha, two
    ISO dates, none more than ten minutes ahead of the site's clock) and
    stores it on the agent's registry document only when it changed.
  - `checkAgentHealth` reads `main`'s commits under `lab-host/` and
    `vps-agent/` from GitHub's public REST API once an hour, from the oldest
    commit an active host reports, into `admin_config/lab_drift`
    (`functions/src/lib/labs/drift.js`), through the Drafts import's pinned,
    redirect-refusing, size-capped fetch. No token and no new secret: the
    repository is public. The Functions app's own build commit was not used,
    because deploys are by hand and say nothing about `main`. A failed read
    keeps the last list and records why (`RATE_LIMITED`, `TIMEOUT`, …), and
    the run's marks and messages come first and never wait on it.
  - Two Health Hub probes, recorded by the health pulse every five minutes
    and shown by the Labs snapshot, judged by the same functions
    (`functions/src/lib/labs/lab-checks.js`): **Lab host runs main**
    (`lab-drift`) is critical once a host-path commit has waited more than
    24 hours unapplied, or when an active host has never reported a commit;
    **Coder template published** (`coder-template`) is critical when the
    template Coder serves is not the converged commit's, from two digests
    the host's daily Coder upkeep report now carries (`templateDigest`, what
    `push-template` last published; `templateSourceDigest`, the checkout
    now), and when the automation never published one. A stale read of
    `main`, or a report without the digests, is unknown, never healthy.
  - The Labs **Agents** tab shows each host's `commit <8 hex> · converged
    <time>` and the drift verdict, in its colour.

- **Eleven alert rules for what the estate collected and nothing paged on
  (PLAT-4, #964).** All route to `ag-plat-prod-cus-01`, and all read data
  that already arrives, so none adds ingestion.
  - `alert-timer-overdue`: one rule over all 25 timers, one alert per timer
    through a `timer` dimension, firing when a timer due at least 45 minutes
    ago has no successful request row since. The schedules live in
    `local.timer_schedules` (period and anchor). The new
    `functions/src/functions/timer-alert-schedules.test.js` holds that map to
    the real `app.timer()` registrations, to each NCRONTAB and to
    `function-inventory.json`. More than five overdue at once collapse into
    one alert, and the rule is quiet while no request telemetry arrives at
    all, so a capped workspace or a dead host does not send 25 mails and 25
    texts.
  - `alert-lab-agent-offline`: `checkAgentHealth`'s decision to tell the
    owner an agent has been offline five minutes, so the owner hears by mail
    and SMS when Telegram is what failed. The nightly reboot does not fire it.
  - `alert-jobs-poison`: a successful `PutMessage` to `platform-jobs-poison`,
    from the storage queue logs already shipped.
  - `alert-swa-bandwidth`: a metric alert on the Static Web App's `BytesSent`
    over a day, at a pace that would use 80% of the Free plan's 100 GB month.
  - `alert-kv-errors` and `alert-kv-data-write`: Key Vault requests answering
    400 or above (past the routine 401 challenge and unseeded-secret 404s),
    and data-plane secret or key writes by anyone but the Function App, on
    both vaults.
  - `alert-kv-config-write`, `alert-rbac-write-app` and
    `alert-rbac-write-mgmt`: Activity Log alerts, which are free and need no
    export, for Resource Manager writes to either vault and role assignment
    or definition changes in both subscriptions.
  - `alert-lab-vault-unwrap`: the seal key wrapped or unwrapped from an
    address the lab host has not heartbeated from, read from the host's own
    `Heartbeat` rows rather than copied from the `hcw-lab` workspace.
  - `alert-lab-ssh-burst`: failed SSH lines in 15 minutes at least 50 and
    four times the day's quarter-hour average.
  - Each create is declared in `scripts/assert-expected-plan.mjs`.
    `kql-alert-columns.test.mjs` now reads every `.tf` file, not
    `observability.tf` alone. `terraform-identity-grants.test.mjs` classifies
    the Activity Log alert and admits a whole subscription in its `scopes`
    only (read, not written; ADR 0005's step-two table records it). Every
    query was parsed and type-checked with Microsoft's Kusto.Language
    parser. Estimated cost is about USD 4.70 a month. The alerting runbook's
    new *The PLAT-4 rules* section has the operator table, three pre-apply
    checks, a fire test for each rule and a fire record. A daily digest of
    denials needs code and is left as a follow-up.

  allow-same-origin allow-forms allow-downloads` and the report bundle saves

  standard, the program package and the decisions index record the
  confirmation; `[REVIEW REQUIRED]` remains only on the per-AddOn
  human-verification widgets, which the owner creates.
- **AddOn panes: independently built tools in sandboxed panes on their own
  lab names, starting with the Migration Hub (ADR 0035; the Phase 6
  website pull request of the App-to-AddOn program).** The site gains a
  catalogue of tool add-ons (`frontend/src/data/addons/catalogue.js`: the

  since 2026-10-10), a generic pane page at `/tools/<id>`
  (`pages/tools/AddOnPanePage.jsx`: the status gate, the sandbox and

  message filter with its four states, an allow-listed `navigate`, a
  30-second watchdog, and one sentence for every way the tool can be

  and one exact origin per available row in the CSP's `frame-src`.
  `/tools/migration` goes from a placeholder to the pane. The Function App
  gains `GET /api/public/addons/{id}/status` (`lib/addons/`): ids closed in
  a server-side registry, a 5-second https-only read of the add-on's
  `/api/health`, a one-minute cache per id with failures cached, and a
  six-field projection that never carries the URL; the address is the
  plain app setting `ADDON_MIGRATION_URL` in Terraform. Admin gains the
  Tool add-ons group with the Migration add-on card, probe and directory
  row, and the Credentials register lists the add-on's vault key. The lab
  host gains the generic `addons` Ansible role (one hardened container per
  `group_vars` row by digest on the loopback, a Caddy route per name with
  the site's sentence at 503, a per-name direct-visit redirect whose
  directive ordering `caddy adapt` checks in CI, the end-of-run privilege
  checks extended to each container) and the migration row, with the
  digest and the widget's site key marked `[VERIFY]` for the owner. The
  AddOn integration standard lands in `docs/standards/`, the program
  package in `docs/architecture/app-to-addon/`, and ADR 0035 records the
  model with two items for the owner's review. Review round 1 (Copilot):
  the add-on containers run on their own bridge network with
  inter-container communication off and egress limited in `DOCKER-USER` to
  the verification endpoint's published ranges on 443 (also written to
  ufw's `after.rules` for the next boot); no volume or mount, compared
  strictly; a row with no digest answers 503 directly and any container
  left from an earlier digest is removed; the privilege checks assert the
  network, the one loopback binding and no mounts, null-safe; the status
  proxy validates the whole version string, shares one in-flight read per
  id, and logs by setting name, class and code only (the minute cache's
  warnings too); the pane focuses its frame on load; the migration row
  ships without `downloads` until ADR 0035 decision 9 is confirmed.
- **Credentials: one register of every credential, with its age and expiry,
  on Admin → Integrations → Credentials, and a Telegram reminder for each
  one only the owner can renew (#1026).** `functions/src/lib/credentials/`
  holds a static register of every credential by name and metadata only —
  where each lives, what uses it, its issuer, whether it renews itself
  (`self`, `automation`, `hand`, or `none` for an identifier) and, where a
  rule exists, its lifetime: Key Vault (built from `secret-catalog.js` so
  the two cannot drift, which `register.test.js` holds), the three MCP
  OAuth connections in `mcp_servers`, the GitHub Actions and Agents
  secrets, the OIDC federations, the HCP Terraform variables of
  `hcw/hcw-azure` and `hcw/hcw-lab`, the Static Web Apps deployment token,
  the Entra and Docker identities, and the lab host's vault keys, files and
  the owner's password-manager entries. `GET /api/cms/credentials`
  (super_admin) merges in the live dates — the Keys tab's `lastWriteAt`,
  the lab host's Coder token report, each MCP connection's state, read as
  a Cosmos projection so no token field is ever fetched — and answers each
  credential's age, expiry (reported, or the last rotation plus its rule
  for a hand-renewed one), and a state: ok, due soon, overdue (red), or
  unknown. A source that cannot be read, or is present but malformed, is
  never read as empty: the credentials that depend on it show unknown, with
  no expiry or reminder. `PUT /api/cms/credentials` records, under the
  document's ETag, when a hand-renewed credential the site cannot read was
  last rotated (`admin_config/credential_register`, a date per credential).
  Every hand credential with a rotation rule gets the reminder row
  `credential-<id>` on the existing Reminders sheet, said by the existing
  `sendReminders` timer: the Anthropic key, the Telegram bot token, both
  GitHub App private keys and the Coder GitHub OAuth secret (every 180
  days, the owner's rule of 2026-10-09), the Static Web Apps token's 90-day
  reset and the two 730-day lab host certificates. With a known date it is
  "Rotate …" at the due date; without one it is "Record when … was last
  rotated", due the day it was added, until the date is recorded. The sync
  owns only those rows: the owner's own reminders pass through untouched,
  the timer's stamps are kept while a row's due date and title stand and
  reset when either changes, and every attempt re-reads the sheet and then
  the dates and writes under the sheet's ETag, so a rotation recorded
  mid-sync is never overwritten. Recording the rotation is the only way a
  register row's cycle ends: the sync reopens one found marked done, the
  Platform Settings save (editor) carries every `credential-` row through
  exactly as stored and cannot add, change or remove one, and the Reminders
  sheet shows them read-only, "Managed by Integrations → Credentials". It
  runs when a rotation is recorded, from the tab's Update reminders
  (`POST /api/cms/credentials/reminders`), and at the start of every
  `sendReminders` run. No value is read, stored or returned anywhere.
  `sendReminders` also binds each Telegram stamp to the cycle it was said
  for, the row's due date and title: after an ETag conflict it re-applies a
  stamp only to a row still in that cycle, so a reminder re-dated or
  renamed meanwhile is said afresh. This applies to every reminder, and
  nothing changes when there is no conflict. A Platform Settings save of the
  sheet is written under the ETag of the read it merged from (412 or 409
  re-reads, three attempts, then 409), so a sync or a stamp that lands
  between the read and the write is never written over. A Keys-tab write
  syncs the credential reminders at once, so a rotation moves its reminder
  without waiting for the timer, and the register copies only `lastWriteAt`
  and `rotatedOn` out of the records it reads. An editor's save of the sheet
  may hold at most 180 of the owner's own reminders: 20 rows stay free for
  the register, so its warnings can always be installed.

- **Lab host: Coder automation. The host renews the site's Coder status
  token and publishes the `hcw-lab` template on its own, with one rotation
  credential the owner seeds once (owner approval 2026-10-08).**
  `hcw-coder-automation-seed` takes the owner's short-lived token on stdin
  and creates the rotation credential: an unscoped, year-long token of
  `hcw-status`, which must be a Template Admin and must not be an Owner, so
  it cannot manage users or act as anyone else. It is a root-only file,
  `/etc/hcw/coder/automation/rotation-token`, not a vault secret, because
  nothing on the host can read HashiCorp Vault unattended (no auth method,
  sealed after a reboot under Shamir keys) and the Ansible vault's password
  is a root-only file beside it. The daily `hcw-coder-automation.timer`
  renews the site's status token when the one the site holds expires within
  30 days or is over 60 days old: a 90-day token with exactly
  `template:read`, `workspace:read`, `api_key:read` and `user:read` (the
  last so the token can read its own expiry, which the site checks), checked against
  Coder, then handed to the site through the lab agent's CLI
  (`vps-agent/bin/report-coder-automation.js`, run with `systemd-run` as
  the agent's user with its `EnvironmentFile`), live only once the CLI
  answers `stored: true`. It deletes `hcw-status`'s older status tokens,
  keeping the newest two, the one before the live one and any younger than
  48 hours, renews the rotation credential under 60 days, and reports
  `checkedAt`, both expiries, the rotation and the template's publish, and a
  content-free `lastError`, every run; a failure fails the unit, which the
  `hcw-unit-failed@` notifier turns into the lab alert. Every `bootstrap.sh`
  run publishes the template with the credential when a file
  `hcw-coder-template-push` copies, or the default autostop, changed since
  its last publish, before `lab_images` removes the old version's images;
  with no credential it says how to seed one and carries on. Coder v2.38's
  token API was read from its docs and source: `lifetime` is a Go duration
  in nanoseconds, no scope means `coder:all`, and a Template Admin's tokens
  may live a year where an Owner's stop at 168 hours. The owner's lines,
  what success looks like and how to rotate by hand are in
  `docs/runbooks/labs-host.md`, "Automatic renewal"; the design is in
  `lab-host/ansible/roles/coder/README.md`, "Coder automation". Tests:
  `lab-host/ansible/roles/coder/tests/hcw-coder-automation.test.py`, run in
  the `ansible-lint (lab-host)` job against a fake Coder API, a fake
  `systemd-run` and a fake site CLI, with no token in any output, state or
  report. The seed keeps a stored credential only while `hcw-status` is
  still a Template Admin and not an Owner, and every run refuses one that
  is not a Template Admin; a new credential that fails before it is stored,
  and that Coder will not delete, is recorded by id and deleted by every
  later run until it is gone (review of #1035). A replaced credential is
  listed the same way, before the new one is written, so an interruption
  cannot leave it usable and forgotten; `hcw-coder-automation revoke`
  turns the automation off by deleting the credential in Coder before the
  file, and comes before any revert of this code; a suspected leak is
  contained on the account, by deleting `hcw-status`, which deletes every
  API key it has, successors included (CodeRabbit, #1035).
- **Coder automation, the site's half: the lab host can hand the site a
  renewed Coder status token through the lab agent, and the site stores it
  only after Coder vouches for it as a working, read-only key of the status
  user; the Hybrid Lab card shows what the host last reported (owner
  approval, 2026-10-08).**
  Until now `CODER-STATUS-TOKEN` was renewed by hand once a year, minted in
  a pane and pasted on the Keys tab, because the host cannot reach Key
  Vault and must not. A fourth agent route, `POST
  /api/agent/reportCoderAutomation`, guarded by `requireAgent` exactly as
  the heartbeat is, takes `{ agentId, statusToken?, report { checkedAt,
  statusTokenExpiresAt?, statusTokenRotatedAt?, rotationTokenExpiresAt?,
  templatePushedAt?, templateVersion?, lastError? } }` and refuses
  anything else with a 400 and a sentence before any read
  (`functions/src/lib/labs/coder-automation.js`, composed in
  `lib/lab-agent.js`). A token must have Coder's key shape, measured
  against Coder v2.38's source (a 10-character id, a dash, a 22-character
  secret), and must pass three reads made with it through `coder-status.js`'s
  guarded GET, each answering exactly 200 (`verifyStatusToken`): the
  running-workspaces read gives an integer count, `GET /api/v2/users/me`
  names `hcw-status` (`CODER_STATUS_USER` may rename it), and the token's
  own key record lists `template:read`, `workspace:read` and
  `api_key:read`, with `user:read` the one more it may carry. An unscoped
  key (`coder:all`, or `all` in the deprecated `scope`), a key with any
  other scope, and another user's key are refused, so a working Template
  Admin key cannot become the read-only status token. Only then is it
  written by `writeCatalogSecret`, the Keys tab's own writer factored out of
  `admin-secrets.js`, so the Keys row goes amber and then green as for a
  paste and there is no second vault client. The writer never throws past
  the vault write and says `vaultWritten`, so a failure after it is answered
  200 `{ ok: true, stored: true }` with the failure as `lastError`, and the
  host does not mint again. The `secret_state` document the Keys tab, the
  agent and every key verdict share is now written one secret's record at a
  time under its ETag (`updateSecretRecord`), so a verdict landing during a
  renewal is no longer lost. One `coder_status_token_rotated` audit row,
  never the value. A token that fails a check is 422 with a sentence naming
  the check, and a vault refusal 502; the report is recorded either way in
  one `admin_config/coder_automation` document, merged under its ETag (event
  dates kept when a report omits them, `lastError` cleared by a clean check,
  anything shaped like a Coder key in it removed). A `checkedAt`,
  `statusTokenRotatedAt` or `templatePushedAt` more than ten minutes ahead
  of the site's clock is a 400, and the card measures silence from the
  site's own `reportedAt`, so a host clock in the future cannot hide a host
  that has stopped. Warning and error lines name a status, never the token,
  the agent or a document id.
  `GET /api/cms/labs/coder-automation` (editor) serves the document, and
  the Hybrid Lab card on the Services tab now groups its keys: Coder's two
  values together with **Automatic renewal** (status token renewed on,
  rotation credential expires on, template last published, last check, and
  `lastError` amber or red by `lib/status.js`), Turnstile's apart. Before
  the first report it reads `Automatic renewal not set up yet`, and the
  manual paste on the Keys tab is unchanged. On the host side,
  `vps-agent/bin/report-coder-automation.js` reads one JSON object on
  stdin, adds `agentId`, posts it with the agent's API client, prints
  `{"ok":true,"stored":<bool>}`, and on failure prints the error's class
  alone; the agent's configuration moved to `vps-agent/lib/config.js` so
  the agent and the one-shot read it one way. `lab-host/README.md`, "The
  status token for the site", gains a paragraph naming the three checks,
  saying the host should mint with `--scope user:read` as well (from Coder
  v2.38's source: both identity reads load the caller's user through its
  authorizing store; not yet measured on the lab's Coder), and pointing to
  the host's setup. Tests: `functions/src/lib/labs/coder-automation.test.js`,
  `coder-status.test.js`, `admin-secrets.test.js`, `key-verdict.test.js`,
  `lab-agent.test.js`;
  `frontend/src/components/admin/integrations/coderAutomationView.test.js`,
  `IntegrationsServices.test.jsx`, `serviceRegistry.test.js`;
  `vps-agent/lib/report-coder-automation.test.js`, `config.test.js`,
  `api.test.js`.
- **CodeRabbit is configured for this repository, for its free open-source
  plan.** It reviews nothing until the CodeRabbit GitHub App is installed on
  the repository, an owner step. `.coderabbit.yaml` at the root (owner
  request, 2026-10-08) enables no paid
  add-on, and every key and value was checked against CodeRabbit's
  `schema.v2.json`. It reviews drafts too, with the `chill` profile and no
  request-changes gate, and it skips lockfiles, build output,
  `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/history/`. It reads the repository's own review
  checklist in `.github/skills/code-review/` as its code guidelines, with
  short path instructions for the functions, infra, lab-host, public-page and
  docs rules. On the open-source plan a public repository with few stars is
  reviewed when asked: comment `@coderabbitai review` on the pull request.
  `scripts/validate-repository-structure.ps1` allows the file at the root.

- **Publer MCP: `PUBLER_API_KEY` usable as an MCP key, bound to
  `mcp.publer.com` only, a server-side MCP tool allowlist that keeps
  Publer's write tools out of reach (#995), a disabled `Publer MCP` seed
  entry, and a Publer runbook with the 2026-10-07 readiness check (nothing
  published).**
  `functions/src/lib/ai/mcp-policy.js` refused `PUBLER_API_KEY` as an MCP
  key name, so Publer's MCP server could not be registered with the key the
  Social Hub already holds. The name is now on the allowlist with
  `mcp.publer.com` as its one host (`app.publer.com`, the REST host, stays
  `publerProxy`'s and is refused for an MCP server), and a URL on that host
  may carry no query string, because Publer's settings page hands out its
  server URL with the key as `?api_key=`, which would otherwise sit in
  Cosmos, in every read of the server list and in the audit row. No header
  code: Publer's server accepts the resolver's plain `Bearer`, and a Sync
  through the repository's own path reached its 47 tools. The AI Engine
  seed gains `publer-mcp`, switched off, written the first time a
  super_admin opens the MCP Servers tab, with a setup page.
  `docs/runbooks/publer.md` records the transport, the auth shape, which
  tools read and which write, and the owner's read-only verification
  (`get_publer_user`). **Tool allowlist (#995):** an MCP server may carry
  `allowedTools`, and `callMcpTool` (so `mcpProxy` and the platform jobs)
  refuses any other tool with 403, naming the tool and the server, before
  any upstream request and whatever the caller's role. A server using
  `PUBLER_API_KEY` must carry a non-empty list: saving one without it is
  refused and a stored one without it refuses every call. The seed's list
  is Publer's 27 read and 7 session tools, never the 13 that create,
  schedule, publish, edit, delete or upload. Writing `allowedTools`, and
  switching a `PUBLER_API_KEY` server on or off, need `super_admin`; a PUT
  that omits the list keeps the stored one; Sync never touches it; the
  `ai_config_updated` audit row records it before and after. Firecrawl,
  Replicate, the VPS token and keyless servers carry no list and still
  accept any tool name, as before. The MCP card reads "34 of 47 tools
  allowed". Tests: `functions/src/lib/ai/mcp.test.js`,
  `functions/src/lib/admin-integrations.test.js`, and
  `frontend/src/lib/aiEngine.test.js` (the seed against the API policy).
